Scattered Spider has manually deleted emails notifying users of suspicious account activity.

techniques.name: Clear Persistence
techniques.summary: Adversaries may clear artifacts associated with previously established persistence on a host system to remove evidence of their activity.

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has removed persistence within victim devices through disabling and uninstalling artifacts. Salt Typhoon has leveraged the commands `guestshell disable` and `guestshell destroy` to deactivate and uninstall Guest Shell contai...
SUNBURST removed IFEO registry values to clean up traces of persistence.
MCMD has the ability to remove set Registry Keys, including those used for persistence.
Bazar's loader can delete scheduled tasks created by a previous instance of the malware.

techniques.name: Relocate Malware
techniques.summary: Once a payload is delivered, adversaries may reproduce copies of the same malware on the victim system to remove evidence of their presence and/or avoid defenses.

procedures.text: BRICKSTORM has copied itself to the `usr/sbin/` folder.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

procedures.text: Hildegard has used an IRC channel for C2 communications.
Magic Hound malware has used IRC for C2.
Adversaries can also use NETEAGLE to establish an RDP connection with a controller over TCP/7519.
Rocke issued wget requests from infected systems to the C2.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

techniques.name: File Transfer Protocols
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with transferring files to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

procedures.text: PoetRAT has used FTP for C2 communications.

APT41 used exploit payloads that initiate download via ftp.
Mythic supports SMB-based peer-to-peer C2 profiles.

techniques.name: Mail Protocols
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with electronic mail delivery to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

procedures.text: ComRAT can use email attachments for command and control.
LightNeuron uses SMTP for C2.
CORESHELL can communicate over SMTP and POP3 for C2.
BadPatch uses SMTP for C2.

techniques.name: DNS
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) application layer protocol to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

procedures.text: Goopy has the ability to communicate with its C2 over DNS.
QUADAGENT uses DNS for C2 communications.
Denis has used DNS tunneling for C2 communications.
SysUpdate has used DNS TXT requests as for its C2 communication.

techniques.name: Publish/Subscribe Protocols
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate using publish/subscribe (pub/sub) application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic.

procedures.text: GLOOXMAIL communicates to servers operated by Google using the Jabber/XMPP protocol for C2.

techniques.name: Software Deployment Tools

Mustang Panda has leveraged legitimate software tools such as AntiVirus Agents, Security Services, and App Development tools to execute scripts and to side-load dlls.

techniques.name: Data Staged
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stage collected data in a central location or directory prior to Exfiltration. Data may be kept in separate files or combined into one file through techniques such as Archive Collected Data.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has collected and staged credentials and network enumeration information, using the networkdll and psfin TrickBot modules.
Volt Typhoon has staged collected data in password-protected archives.
VOID MANTICORE has staged compressed files in specified locations prior to exfiltration over C2.
INC Ransom has staged data on compromised hosts prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Local Data Staging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stage collected data in a central location or directory on the local system prior to Exfiltration.

procedures.text: Storm-1811 has locally staged captured credentials for subsequent manual exfiltration.
OopsIE stages the output from command execution and collected files in specific folders before exfiltration.
AuTo Stealer can store collected data from an infected host to a file named `Hostname_UserName.txt` prior to exfiltration.
CHIMNEYSWEEP can store captured screenshots to disk including to a covert store named `APPX.%x%x%x%x%x.tmp` where `%x` is a random value.

techniques.name: Remote Data Staging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stage data collected from multiple systems in a central location or directory on one system prior to Exfiltration.

procedures.text: Chimera has staged stolen data on designated servers in the target environment.
MirrorFace has gathered data and files of interest on a single victim machine.
Sea Turtle staged collected email archives in the public web directory of a website that was accessible from the internet.
ccf32 has copied files to a remote machine infected with Chinoxy or another backdoor.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

procedures.text: APT41 used compromised credentials to log on to other systems.
FIN8 has used valid accounts for persistence and lateral movement.
FIN4 has used legitimate credentials to hijack email communications.
FIN7 has harvested valid administrative credentials for lateral movement.

techniques.name: Default Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a default account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

procedures.text: FIN13 has leveraged default credentials for authenticating myWebMethods (WMS) and QLogic web management interface to gain initial access.
UNC3886 has harvested and used vCenter Server service accounts.
HyperStack can use default credentials to connect to IPC$ shares on remote machines.
Magic Hound enabled and used the default system managed account, DefaultAccount, via `"powershell.exe" /c net user DefaultAccount /active:yes` to connect to a targeted Exchange server over RDP.

techniques.name: Domain Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a domain account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

procedures.text: CreepySnail can use stolen credentials to authenticate on target networks.
Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a domain user account.
Naikon has used administrator credentials for lateral movement in compromised networks.
Agrius attempted to acquire valid credentials for victim environments through various means to enable follow-on lateral movement.

techniques.name: Local Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

procedures.text: Kimsuky has used a tool called GREASE to add a Windows admin account in order to allow them continued access via RDP.
Emotet can brute force a local admin password, then use it to facilitate lateral movement.
Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a local user account.
PROMETHIUM has created admin accounts on a compromised host.

techniques.name: Cloud Accounts
techniques.summary: Valid accounts in cloud environments may allow adversaries to perform actions to achieve Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

procedures.text: APT29 has gained access to a global administrator account in Azure AD and has used `Service Principal` credentials in Exchange.
NIMBUS MANTICORE has gained access to Azure AD Connect accounts to modify permissions and to create accounts for persistence.
Shai-Hulud has leveraged compromised accounts to log into cloud services to access cloud hosted repositories.
APT5 has accessed Microsoft M365 cloud environments using stolen credentials.

techniques.name: Taint Shared Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deliver payloads to remote systems by adding content to shared storage locations, such as network drives or internal code repositories.

procedures.text: H1N1 has functionality to copy itself to network shares.
Darkhotel used a virus that propagates by infecting executables stored on shared drives.
RedCurl has placed modified LNK files on network drives for lateral movement.
Ramsay can spread itself by infecting other portable executable files on networks shared drives.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, hotfixes, service packs, and architecture.

procedures.text: Micropsia gathers the hostname and OS version from the victim’s machine.
njRAT enumerates the victim operating system and computer name during the initial infection.
DarkGate will gather various system information such as domain, display adapter description, operating system type and version, processor type, and RAM amount.
Qilin can detect whether a system is running FreeBSD, VMkernel (ESXi), Nutanix AHV, or a standard Linux distribution to enable platform-specific encryption behaviors.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or may search in specific locations of a host or network share for certain information within a file system.

procedures.text: BLACKCOFFEE has the capability to enumerate files.
Orz can gather victim drive information.
Attor has a plugin that enumerates files with specific extensions on all hard disk drives and stores file information in encrypted log files.
USBStealer searches victim drives for files matching certain extensions (“.skr”,“.pkr” or “.key”) or names.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment.

procedures.text: Aquatic Panda used the last command in Linux environments to identify recently logged-in users on victim machines.
Scattered Spider has identified vSphere administrator accounts.
ShimRatReporter listed all non-privileged and privileged accounts available on the machine.
Woody RAT can identify administrator accounts on an infected machine.

techniques.name: Local Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts. This information can help adversaries determine which local accounts exist on a system to aid in follow-on behavior.

procedures.text: USBferry can use net user to gather information about local accounts.
Agent Tesla can collect account information from the victim’s machine.
Kwampirs collects a list of accounts with the command net users .
Ke3chang performs account discovery using commands such as net localgroup administrators and net group "REDACTED" /domain on specific permissions groups.

techniques.name: Domain Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.

procedures.text: DUSTTRAP can enumerate domain accounts.
SoreFang can enumerate domain accounts via net.exe user /domain .
Net commands used with the /domain flag can be used to gather information about and manipulate user accounts on the current domain.
FIN13 can identify user accounts associated with a Service Principal Name and query Service Principal Names within the domain by utilizing the following scripts: `GetUserSPNs.vbs` and `querySpn.vbs`.

techniques.name: Email Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of email addresses and accounts. Adversaries may try to dump Exchange address lists such as global address lists (GALs).

procedures.text: TA505 has used the tool EmailStealer to steal and send lists of e-mail addresses to a remote server.
Magic Hound has used Powershell to discover email accounts.
Grandoreiro can parse Outlook .pst files to extract e-mail addresses.
RedCurl has collected information about email accounts.

techniques.name: Cloud Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of cloud accounts.

procedures.text: Storm-0501 has conducted enumeration of users, roles, and resources within victim Azure tenants using the tool Azurehound.
ROADTools can enumerate Azure AD users.
Mini Shai-Hulud has enumerated cloud accounts and subscriptions accessible to the targeted identity.
AADInternals can enumerate Azure AD users.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications to a command and control server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure.

procedures.text: Sagerunex uses several proxy configuration settings to ensure connectivity.
NETWIRE can implement use of proxies to pivot traffic.
ZIPLINE can create a proxy server on compromised hosts.
RansomHub can use a proxy to connect to remote SFTP servers.

techniques.name: Internal Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an internal proxy to direct command and control traffic between two or more systems in a compromised environment.

procedures.text: Velvet Ant has tunneled traffic from victims through an internal, compromised host to proxy communications to command and control nodes.
Pay2Key has designated machines in the compromised network to serve as reverse proxy pivot points to channel communications with C2.
Duqu can be configured to have commands relayed over a peer-to-peer network of infected hosts if some of the hosts do not have Internet access.
CHOPSTICK used a proxy server between victims and the C2 server.

techniques.name: External Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an external proxy to act as an intermediary for network communications to a command and control server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure.

procedures.text: QUIETEXIT can proxy traffic via SOCKS.
APT39 has used various tools to proxy C2 communications.
ShimRat can use pre-configured HTTP proxies.
QakBot has a module that can proxy C2 communications.

techniques.name: Multi-hop Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may chain together multiple proxies to disguise the source of malicious traffic.

procedures.text: Keydnap uses a copy of tor2web proxy for HTTPS communications.
MacSpy uses Tor for command and control.
GreyEnergy has used Tor relays for Command and Control servers.
Ember Bear has configured multi-hop proxies via ProxyChains within victim environments.

techniques.name: Domain Fronting
techniques.summary: Adversaries may take advantage of routing schemes in Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) and other services which host multiple domains to obfuscate the intended destination of HTTPS traffic or traffic tunneled through H...

procedures.text: Cobalt Strike has the ability to accept a value for HTTP Host Header to enable domain fronting.
APT29 has used the meek domain fronting plugin for Tor to hide the destination of C2 traffic.
meek uses Domain Fronting to disguise the destination of network traffic as another server that is hosted in the same Content Delivery Network (CDN) as the intended destination.
Mythic supports domain fronting via custom request headers.

Gamaredon Group has replicated to removable media by leveraging the User Assist Reg Key and creating LNKs on all network and removable drives available on the infected host.

techniques.name: Communication Through Removable Media
techniques.summary: Adversaries can perform command and control between compromised hosts on potentially disconnected networks using removable media to transfer commands from system to system.

procedures.text: Part of APT28's operation involved using CHOPSTICK modules to copy itself to air-gapped machines, using files written to USB sticks to transfer data and command traffic.

USBStealer drops commands for a second victim onto a removable media drive inserted into the first victim, and commands are executed when the drive is inserted into the second victim.

techniques.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an OSI non-application layer protocol for communication between host and C2 server or among infected hosts within a network.

procedures.text: FRP can communicate over TCP, TCP stream multiplexing, KERN Communications Protocol (KCP), QUIC, and UDP.
OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D has used a custom binary protocol over port 443 for C2 traffic.
Anchor has used ICMP in C2 communications.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain and/or elevate access to victim systems.

techniques.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may add adversary-controlled credentials to a cloud account to maintain persistent access to victim accounts and instances within the environment.

techniques.name: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may grant additional permission levels to maintain persistent access to an adversary-controlled email account.

techniques.name: Additional Cloud Roles

techniques.name: SSH Authorized Keys
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the SSH authorized_keys file to maintain persistence on a victim host.

Skidmap has the ability to add the public key of its handlers to the authorized_keys file to maintain persistence on an infected host.
Salt Typhoon has added SSH authorized_keys under root or other users at the Linux level on compromised network devices.

XCSSET will create an ssh key if necessary with the ssh-keygen -t rsa -f $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa -P command. XCSSET will upload a private key file to the server to remotely access the host without a password.

techniques.name: Device Registration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may register a device to an adversary-controlled account.

procedures.text: APT29 has enrolled their own devices into compromised cloud tenants, including enrolling a device in MFA to an Azure AD environment following a successful password guessing attack against a dormant account.
AADInternals can register a device to Azure AD.

techniques.name: Additional Container Cluster Roles
techniques.summary: An adversary may add additional roles or permissions to an adversary-controlled user or service account to maintain persistent access to a container orchestration system.

techniques.name: Additional Local or Domain Groups
techniques.summary: An adversary may add additional local or domain groups to an adversary-controlled account to maintain persistent access to a system or domain.

procedures.text: SMOKEDHAM has added user accounts to local Admin groups.
APT41 has added user accounts to the User and Admin groups.
APT3 has been known to add created accounts to local admin groups to maintain elevated access.
The `net localgroup` and `net group` commands in Net can be used to add existing users to local and domain groups.

techniques.name: Web Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for relaying data to/from a compromised system.

procedures.text: Nightdoor can utilize Microsoft OneDrive or Google Drive for command and control purposes.
Latrodectus has used Google Firebase to download malicious installation scripts.
RedCurl has used web services to download malicious files.
Inception has incorporated at least five different cloud service providers into their C2 infrastructure including CloudMe.

techniques.name: Dead Drop Resolver
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service to host information that points to additional command and control (C2) infrastructure.

procedures.text: Astaroth can store C2 information on cloud hosting services such as AWS and CloudFlare and websites like YouTube and Facebook.
BADNEWS collects C2 information via a dead drop resolver.
The KEYPLUG Windows variant has retrieved C2 addresses from encoded data in posts on tech community forums.
Some MiniDuke components use Twitter to initially obtain the address of a C2 server or as a backup if no hard-coded C2 server responds.

techniques.name: Bidirectional Communication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to and receiving output from a compromised system over the Web service channel.

procedures.text: PowerStallion uses Microsoft OneDrive as a C2 server via a network drive mapped with net use .
BoxCaon has used DropBox for C2 communications.
RIFLESPINE can retrieve C2 commands from an encrypted file on Google Drive then upload the results of command execution back to Google Drive.
Crutch can use Dropbox to receive commands and upload stolen data.

techniques.name: One-Way Communication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service as a means for sending commands to a compromised system without receiving return output over the Web service channel.

procedures.text: EVILNUM has used a one-way communication method via GitLab and Digital Point to perform C2.
Leviathan has received C2 instructions from user profiles created on legitimate websites such as Github and TechNet.
Gamaredon Group has used Telegram Messenger content to discover the IP address for C2 communications.
Sagerunex has used web services such as Twitter for command and control purposes.

techniques.name: Multi-Stage Channels
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create multiple stages for command and control that are employed under different conditions or for certain functions.

procedures.text: An APT3 downloader first establishes a SOCKS5 connection to 192.157.198[.]103 using TCP port 1913; once the server response is verified, it then requests a connection to 192.184.60[.]229 on TCP port 81.
LunarWeb can use one C2 URL for first contact and to upload information about the host computer and two additional C2 URLs for getting commands.

BLACKCOFFEE uses Microsoft’s TechNet Web portal to obtain an encoded tag containing the IP address of a command and control server and then communicates separately with that IP address for C2. If the C2 server is discovered or shut down,...
Lazarus Group has used multi-stage malware components that inject later stages into separate processes.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.summary: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

procedures.text: Fox Kitten has downloaded additional tools including PsExec directly to endpoints.
EvilBunny has downloaded additional Lua scripts from the C2.
Pandora can load additional drivers and files onto a victim machine.
ShimRat can download additional files.

techniques.name: Native API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to execute behaviors.

procedures.text: EvilBunny has used various API calls as part of its checks to see if the malware is running in a sandbox.
Exbyte calls `ShellExecuteW` with the `IpOperation` parameter `RunAs` to launch `explorer.exe` with elevated privileges.
Winnti for Windows can use Native API to create a new process and to start services.
Pony has used several Windows functions for various purposes.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.

procedures.text: Fox Kitten has brute forced RDP credentials.
HEXANE has used brute force attacks to compromise valid credentials.
Chaos conducts brute force attacks against SSH services to gain initial access.
Caterpillar WebShell has a module to perform brute force attacks on a system.

techniques.name: Password Guessing
techniques.summary: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials within the system or environment may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts.

procedures.text: China Chopper's server component can perform brute force password guessing against authentication portals.
VOID MANTICORE has conducted password guessing to gain initial access.
Emotet has been observed using a hard coded list of passwords to brute force user accounts.
SpeakUp can perform brute forcing using a pre-defined list of usernames and passwords in an attempt to log in to administrative panels.

techniques.name: Password Cracking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use password cracking to attempt to recover usable credentials, such as plaintext passwords, when credential material such as password hashes are obtained.

procedures.text: APT3 has been known to brute force password hashes to be able to leverage plain text credentials.
Net Crawler uses a list of known credentials gathered through credential dumping to guess passwords to accounts as it spreads throughout a network.
Dragonfly has dropped and executed tools used for password cracking, including Hydra and CrackMapExec.

Salt Typhoon has cracked passwords for accounts with weak encryption obtained from the configuration files of compromised network devices. Salt Typhoon has cracked weak hashed passwords stolen from configuration files.

techniques.name: Password Spraying
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.

procedures.text: HAFNIUM has gained initial access through password spray attacks.
Bad Rabbit’s infpub.dat file uses NTLM login credentials to brute force Windows machines.
CrackMapExec can brute force credential authentication by using a supplied list of usernames and a single password.
Linux Rabbit brute forces SSH passwords in order to attempt to gain access and install its malware onto the server.

techniques.name: Credential Stuffing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from breach dumps of unrelated accounts to gain access to target accounts through credential overlap.

procedures.text: Chimera has used credential stuffing against victim's remote services to obtain valid accounts.
TrickBot uses brute-force attack against RDP with rdpscanDll module.
VOID MANTICORE has utilized credential stuffing attacks to obtain initial access to victim environments.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms, (i.e., smart cards, token generators, etc.) to gain access to credentials that can be used to access systems, services, and network resources.

procedures.text: SLOWPULSE can log credentials on compromised Pulse Secure VPNs during the `DSAuth::AceAuthServer::checkUsernamePassword`ACE-2FA authentication procedure.
Sykipot is known to contain functionality that enables targeting of smart card technologies to proxy authentication for connections to restricted network resources using detected hardware tokens.
Kimsuky has used a proprietary tool to intercept one time passwords required for two-factor authentication.
evilginx2 can intercept authentication tokens to enable bypass of non-phishing resistant forms of MFA.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.summary: Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry as part of a variety of other techniques to aid in defense evasion, persistence, and execution.

procedures.text: CharmPower can remove persistence-related artifacts from the Registry.
Turla has modified Registry values to store payloads.
PlugX has a module to create, delete, or modify Registry keys.
ShadowPad can modify the Registry to store and maintain a configuration block and virtual file system.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to take screen captures of the desktop to gather information over the course of an operation.

procedures.text: The AshTag AshenOrchestrator component has the ability to take screenshots.
Pteranodon can capture screenshots at a configurable interval.
VOID MANTICORE has captured screen content during an active Zoom session.
GRIFFON has used a screenshot module that can be used to take a screenshot of the remote system.

techniques.name: Email Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target user email to collect sensitive information. Emails may contain sensitive data, including trade secrets or personal information, that can prove valuable to adversaries.

procedures.text: Ember Bear attempts to collect mail from accessed systems and servers.
Silent Librarian has exfiltrated entire mailboxes from compromised accounts.
Emotet has been observed leveraging a module that can scrape email addresses from Outlook.
Magic Hound has compromised email credentials in order to steal sensitive data.

techniques.name: Local Email Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target user email on local systems to collect sensitive information. Files containing email data can be acquired from a user’s local system, such as Outlook storage or cache files.

procedures.text: LunarMail can capture the recipients of sent email messages from compromised accounts.
WIRTE has collected documents from victims' email accounts.
RedCurl has collected emails to use in future phishing campaigns.
Smoke Loader searches through Outlook files and directories (e.g., inbox, sent, templates, drafts, archives, etc.).

techniques.name: Remote Email Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target an Exchange server, Office 365, or Google Workspace to collect sensitive information.

procedures.text: Ke3chang has used compromised credentials and a .NET tool to dump data from Microsoft Exchange mailboxes.
MailSniper can be used for searching through email in Exchange and Office 365 environments.
APT28 has collected emails from victim Microsoft Exchange servers.
VOID MANTICORE has gathered victim email-content from victim servers.

techniques.name: Email Forwarding Rule
techniques.summary: Adversaries may setup email forwarding rules to collect sensitive information.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has redirected emails notifying users of suspicious account activity.
Silent Librarian has set up auto forwarding rules on compromised e-mail accounts.
LAPSUS$ has set an Office 365 tenant level mail transport rule to send all mail in and out of the targeted organization to the newly created account.
Star Blizzard has abused email forwarding rules to monitor the activities of a victim, steal information, and maintain persistent access after compromised credentials are reset.

techniques.name: Clipboard Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect data stored in the clipboard from users copying information within or between applications. For example, on Windows adversaries can access clipboard data by using clip.exe or Get-Clipboard .

procedures.text: Agent Tesla can steal data from the victim’s clipboard.
APT39 has used tools capable of stealing contents of the clipboard.
RTM collects data from the clipboard.
SILENTTRINITY can monitor Clipboard text and can use `System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard.GetText()` to collect data from the clipboard.

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.summary: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.

procedures.text: VOID MANTICORE conducted large-scale data exfiltration in the Stryker operation, consistent with automated or scripted collection against enterprise systems.

T9000 searches removable storage devices for files with a pre-defined list of file extensions (e.g. .doc, .ppt, .xls, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx). Any matching files are encrypted and written to a local user directory.
Rover automatically collects files from the local system and removable drives based on a predefined list of file extensions on a regular timeframe.
Micropsia executes an RAR tool to recursively archive files based on a predefined list of file extensions (.xls, .xlsx, .csv, .odt, .doc, .docx, .ppt, .pptx, .pdf, .mdb, .accdb, .accde, *.txt).

techniques.name: Peripheral Device Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about attached peripheral devices and components connected to a computer system.

procedures.text: INC Ransomware can identify external USB and hard drives for encryption and printers to print ransom notes.
Equation has used tools with the functionality to search for specific information about the attached hard drive that could be used to identify and overwrite the firmware.
APT37 has a Bluetooth device harvester, which uses Windows Bluetooth APIs to find information on connected Bluetooth devices.
jRAT can map UPnP ports.

techniques.name: Audio Capture
techniques.summary: An adversary can leverage a computer's peripheral devices (e.g., microphones and webcams) or applications (e.g., voice and video call services) to capture audio recordings for the purpose of listening into sensitive c...

procedures.text: Flame can record audio using any existing hardware recording devices.
ROKRAT has an audio capture and eavesdropping module.
Bandook has modules that are capable of capturing audio.
VOID MANTICORE has gathered audio during a Zoom session.

techniques.name: System Time Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may gather the system time and/or time zone settings from a local or remote system. The system time is set and stored by services, such as the Windows Time Service on Windows or systemsetup on macOS.

procedures.text: Shamoon obtains the system time and will only activate if it is greater than a preset date.
ShrinkLocker retrieves a system timestamp that is used in generating an encryption key.
Astaroth collects the timestamp from the infected machine.
Zebrocy gathers the current time zone and date information from the system.

techniques.name: Video Capture
techniques.summary: An adversary can leverage a computer's peripheral devices (e.g., integrated cameras or webcams) or applications (e.g., video call services) to capture video recordings for the purpose of gathering information.

procedures.text: Empire can capture webcam data on Windows and macOS systems.
Clambling can record screen content in AVI format.
Crimson can capture webcam video on targeted systems.
TajMahal has the ability to capture webcam video.

techniques.name: Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may take advantage of trusted developer utilities to proxy execution of malicious payloads.

techniques.name: MSBuild
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use MSBuild to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility. MSBuild.exe (Microsoft Build Engine) is a software build platform used by Visual Studio.

procedures.text: NOOPLDR can be executed via MSBuild.
A version of PlugX loads as shellcode within a .NET Framework project using msbuild.exe, presumably to bypass application control techniques.
Empire can use built-in modules to abuse trusted utilities like MSBuild.exe.

techniques.name: ClickOnce
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use ClickOnce applications (.appref-ms and .application files) to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility.

techniques.name: JamPlus
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use `JamPlus` to proxy the execution of a malicious script. `JamPlus` is a build utility tool for code and data build systems.

techniques.name: Shared Modules
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute malicious payloads via loading shared modules.

procedures.text: gh0st RAT can load DLLs into memory.
Hydraq creates a backdoor through which remote attackers can load and call DLL functions.
PUNCHBUGGY can load a DLL using the LoadLibrary API.
Stuxnet calls LoadLibrary then executes exports from a DLL.

techniques.name: Data Encoding
techniques.summary: Adversaries may encode data to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect. Command and control (C2) information can be encoded using a standard data encoding system.

procedures.text: LAMEHUG can encode queries sent to LLMs.
Velvet Ant sent commands to compromised F5 BIG-IP devices in an encoded format requiring a passkey before interpretation and execution.
After encrypting C2 data, BADNEWS converts it into a hexadecimal representation and then encodes it into base64.
Mythic provides various transform functions to encode and/or randomize C2 data.

techniques.name: Standard Encoding
techniques.summary: Adversaries may encode data with a standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect.

procedures.text: SideTwist has used Base64 for encoded C2 traffic.
Fysbis can use Base64 to encode its C2 traffic.
DnsSystem can Base64 encode data sent to C2.
C2 traffic from ADVSTORESHELL is encrypted, then encoded with Base64 encoding.

techniques.name: Non-Standard Encoding
techniques.summary: Adversaries may encode data with a non-standard data encoding system to make the content of command and control traffic more difficult to detect.

procedures.text: OceanSalt can encode data with a NOT operation before sending the data to the control server.
Small Sieve can use a custom hex byte swapping encoding scheme to obfuscate tasking traffic.
TONESHELL has encoded a payload with a random 32-byte key using XOR. TONESHELL has also encoded payloads with a 256-byte key using XOR.
NightClub has used a non-standard encoding in DNS tunneling removing any `=` from the result of base64 encoding, and replacing `/` characters with `-s` and `+` characters with `-p`.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has used open-source tools such as Weave Scope to target exposed Docker API ports and gain initial access to victim environments. TeamTNT has also targeted exposed kubelets for Kubernetes environments.
FIN13 has gained access to compromised environments via remote access services such as the corporate virtual private network (VPN).
Linux Rabbit attempts to gain access to the server via SSH.
Mafalda can establish an SSH connection from a compromised host to a server.

techniques.name: Access Token Manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify access tokens to operate under a different user or system security context to perform actions and bypass access controls.

procedures.text: Qilin can use an embedded Mimikatz module for token manipulation.

HermeticWiper can use `AdjustTokenPrivileges` to grant itself privileges for debugging with `SeDebugPrivilege`, creating backups with `SeBackupPrivilege`, loading drivers with `SeLoadDriverPrivilege`, and shutting down a local system wit...
SUNSPOT modified its security token to grants itself debugging privileges by adding SeDebugPrivilege .
Lotus Blossom has retrieved process tokens for processes to adjust the privileges of the launch process or other items.

techniques.name: Token Impersonation/Theft
techniques.summary: Adversaries may duplicate then impersonate another user's existing token to escalate privileges and bypass access controls.

procedures.text: FinFisher uses token manipulation with NtFilterToken as part of UAC bypass.
CRASHPAD has impersonated the `explorer.exe` user privileges to call Windows API `CryptUnprotectData`.
Emotet has the ability to duplicate the user’s token. For example, Emotet may use a variant of Google’s ProtoBuf to send messages that specify how code will be executed.
Fooder has used the `DuplicateTokenEx` API to duplicate the token of a specified process, and `CreateProcessAsUserA` to execute its payload.

techniques.name: Create Process with Token
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create a new process with an existing token to escalate privileges and bypass access controls.

procedures.text: Azorult can call WTSQueryUserToken and CreateProcessAsUser to start a new process with local system privileges.
Turla RPC backdoors can impersonate or steal process tokens before executing commands.
PipeMon can attempt to gain administrative privileges using token impersonation.
Lazarus Group keylogger KiloAlfa obtains user tokens from interactive sessions to execute itself with API call CreateProcessAsUserA under that user's context.

techniques.name: Make and Impersonate Token
techniques.summary: Adversaries may make new tokens and impersonate users to escalate privileges and bypass access controls.

procedures.text: Mafalda can create a token for a different user.
BlackByte constructed a valid authentication token following Microsoft Exchange exploitation to allow for follow-on privileged command execution.
FIN13 has utilized tools such as Incognito V2 for token manipulation and impersonation.
SILENTTRINITY can make tokens from known credentials.

techniques.name: Parent PID Spoofing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may spoof the parent process identifier (PPID) of a new process to evade process-monitoring defenses or to elevate privileges.

procedures.text: KONNI has used parent PID spoofing to spawn a new `cmd` process using `CreateProcessW` and a handle to `Taskmgr.exe`.
Cobalt Strike can spawn processes with alternate PPIDs.
PipeMon can use parent PID spoofing to elevate privileges.
DarkGate relies on parent PID spoofing as part of its "rootkit-like" functionality to evade detection via Task Manager or Process Explorer.

techniques.name: SID-History Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use SID-History Injection to escalate privileges and bypass access controls. The Windows security identifier (SID) is a unique value that identifies a user or group account.

procedures.text: Mimikatz's MISC::AddSid module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync be...
Empire can add a SID-History to a user if on a domain controller.

techniques.name: Network Share Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may look for folders and drives shared on remote systems as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as a precursor for Collection and to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral M...

procedures.text: BADHATCH can check a user's access to the C$ share on a compromised machine.
BlackByte Ransomware can identify network shares connected to the victim machine.
Ramsay can scan for network drives which may contain documents for collection.
Conti can enumerate remote open SMB network shares using NetShareEnum() .

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems.

procedures.text: Indrik Spider used wmic.exe to add a new user to the system.
LockBit 2.0 has been observed creating accounts for persistence using simple names like "a".
Scattered Spider creates new user identities within the compromised organization.
Salt Typhoon has created Linux-level users on compromised network devices through modification of `/etc/shadow` and `/etc/passwd`.

techniques.name: Local Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has created local administrator accounts to maintain persistence in compromised networks.
APT5 has created Local Administrator accounts to maintain access to systems with short-cycle credential rotation.
HiddenWasp creates a user account as a means to provide initial persistence to the compromised machine.
GoldenSpy can create new users on an infected system.

techniques.name: Domain Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create a domain account to maintain access to victim systems.

procedures.text: Pupy can user PowerView to execute “net user” commands and create domain accounts.
GALLIUM created high-privileged domain user accounts to maintain access to victim networks.
BlackByte created privileged domain accounts during intrusions.
Wizard Spider has created and used new accounts within a victim's Active Directory environment to maintain persistence.

techniques.name: Cloud Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create a cloud account to maintain access to victim systems.

procedures.text: APT29 can create new users through Azure AD.
LAPSUS$ has created global admin accounts in the targeted organization's cloud instances to gain persistence.
AADInternals can create new Azure AD users.

techniques.name: Office Application Startup
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage Microsoft Office-based applications for persistence between startups. Microsoft Office is a fairly common application suite on Windows-based operating systems within an enterprise network.

procedures.text: APT32 have replaced Microsoft Outlook's VbaProject.OTM file to install a backdoor macro for persistence.

Gamaredon Group has inserted malicious macros into existing documents, providing persistence when they are reopened. Gamaredon Group has loaded the group's previously delivered VBA project by relaunching Microsoft Outlook with the /altvb...

techniques.name: Office Template Macros
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Office templates to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Microsoft Office contains templates that are part of common Office applications and are used to customize styles.

procedures.text: MuddyWater has used a Word Template, Normal.dotm, for persistence.
ROAMINGHOUSE has been loaded as a Word Template file when victims opened a decoy document placed in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Templates` alongside a ROAMINGHOUSE macro.
BackConfig has the ability to use hidden columns in Excel spreadsheets to store executable files or commands for VBA macros.
Cobalt Strike has the ability to use an Excel Workbook to execute additional code by enabling Office to trust macros and execute code without user permission.

techniques.name: Office Test
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse the Microsoft Office "Office Test" Registry key to obtain persistence on a compromised system.

procedures.text: APT28 has used the Office Test persistence mechanism within Microsoft Office by adding the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf to execute code.

techniques.name: Outlook Forms
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook forms to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook forms are used as templates for presentation and functionality in Outlook messages.

procedures.text: Ruler can be used to automate the abuse of Outlook Forms to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Outlook Home Page
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook's Home Page feature to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook Home Page is a legacy feature used to customize the presentation of Outlook folders.

procedures.text: OilRig has abused the Outlook Home Page feature for persistence. OilRig has also used CVE-2017-11774 to roll back the initial patch designed to protect against Home Page abuse.
Ruler can be used to automate the abuse of Outlook Home Pages to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Outlook Rules
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Outlook rules to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Outlook rules allow a user to define automated behavior to manage email messages.

procedures.text: Ruler can be used to automate the abuse of Outlook Rules to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Add-ins
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft Office add-ins to obtain persistence on a compromised system. Office add-ins can be used to add functionality to Office programs.

procedures.text: Bisonal has been loaded through a `.wll` extension added to the ` %APPDATA%\microsoft\word\startup\` repository.
Naikon has used the RoyalRoad exploit builder to drop a second stage loader, intel.wll, into the Word Startup folder on the compromised host.
LunarLoader has the ability to use Microsoft Outlook add-ins to establish persistence.
LunarMail has the ability to use Outlook add-ins for persistence.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use Obfuscated Files or Information to hide artifacts of an intrusion from analysis. They may require separate mechanisms to decode or deobfuscate that information depending on how they intend to use it.

procedures.text: PHPsert has the ability to decode and decrypt obfuscated strings prior to execution.
SPAWNCHIMERA has decoded a XOR encoded private key.
ZeroT shellcode decrypts and decompresses its RC4-encrypted payload.
AppleJeus has decoded files received from a C2.

techniques.name: Software Extensions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse software extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems.

techniques.name: Browser Extensions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse internet browser extensions to establish persistent access to victim systems.

procedures.text: Mispadu utilizes malicious Google Chrome browser extensions to steal financial data.
Kimsuky has used Google Chrome browser extensions to infect victims and to steal passwords and cookies.
OSX/Shlayer can install malicious Safari browser extensions to serve ads.
Lumma Stealer has installed a malicious browser extension to target Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera and Brave browsers for the purpose of stealing data.

techniques.name: IDE Extensions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse an integrated development environment (IDE) extension to establish persistent access to victim systems.

procedures.text: Mustang Panda has leveraged Visual Studio Code’s (VSCode) embedded reverse shell feature using the command `code.exe tunnel` to execute code and deliver additional payloads.
TeamPCP has compromised VS Code and Open VSX IDE extensions.

techniques.name: Browser Session Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may take advantage of security vulnerabilities and inherent functionality in browser software to change content, modify user-behaviors, and intercept information as part of various browser session hijackin...

procedures.text: TrickBot uses web injects and browser redirection to trick the user into providing their login credentials on a fake or modified web page.
Dridex can perform browser attacks via web injects to steal information such as credentials, certificates, and cookies.
Carberp has captured credentials when a user performs login through a SSL session.
TRANSLATEXT has the ability to use form-grabbing and event-listening to extract data from web data forms.

techniques.name: Forced Authentication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather credential material by invoking or forcing a user to automatically provide authentication information through a mechanism in which they can intercept.

procedures.text: DarkHydrus used Template Injection to launch an authentication window for users to enter their credentials.

Dragonfly has gathered hashed user credentials over SMB using spearphishing attachments with external resource links and by modifying .LNK file icon resources to collect credentials from virtualized systems.
EnvyScout can use protocol handlers to coax the operating system to send NTLMv2 authentication responses to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access to a system through a user visiting a website over the normal course of browsing.

procedures.text: Transparent Tribe has used websites with malicious hyperlinks and iframes to infect targeted victims with Crimson, njRAT, and other malicious tools.
RTM has distributed its malware via the RIG and SUNDOWN exploit kits, as well as online advertising network Yandex.Direct .
PLATINUM has sometimes used drive-by attacks against vulnerable browser plugins.
Windshift has used compromised websites to register custom URL schemes on a remote system.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. The weakness in the system can be a software bug, a temporary glitch, or a misconfiguration.

procedures.text: Rocke exploited Apache Struts, Oracle WebLogic (CVE-2017-10271), and Adobe ColdFusion (CVE-2017-3066) vulnerabilities to deliver malware.
Threat Group-3390 has exploited the Microsoft SharePoint vulnerability CVE-2019-0604 and CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, and CVE-2021-27065 in Exchange Server.
FIN7 has compromised targeted organizations through exploitation of CVE-2021-31207 in Exchange.

TeamPCP has exploited misconfigurations in GitHub Actions and vulnerabilities such as CVE-2026-33634 in the Aqua Security Trivy scanner and CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell) against vulnerable cloud endpoints.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

procedures.text: Lumma Stealer has been delivered through cracked software downloads.
OilRig has leveraged compromised organizations to conduct supply chain attacks on government entities.
Raccoon Stealer has been distributed through cracked software downloads.

Ember Bear has compromised information technology providers and software developers providing services to targets of interest, building initial access to ultimate victims at least in part through compromise of service providers that work...

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate software dependencies and development tools prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

procedures.text: Tsundere Botnet has used the Node Package Manager (npm) to download malicious packages and to deliver the payload.
BeaverTail has been hosted on code repositories and disseminated to victims through NPM packages.
Shai-Hulud has published itself on compromised code repository maintainers within infected packages in attempts to propagate to other victims. Shai-Hulud has also modified versions of code packages.
TeamPCP has conducted coordinated supply chain attacks targeting open-source developer infrastructure including the NPM, VS Code, Docker, and PyPi ecosystems to compromise multiple software packages.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate application software prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

procedures.text: APT41 gained access to production environments where they could inject malicious code into legitimate, signed files and widely distribute them to end users.
Cobalt Group has compromised legitimate web browser updates to deliver a backdoor.
GOLD SOUTHFIELD has distributed ransomware by backdooring software installers via a strategic web compromise of the site hosting Italian WinRAR.
GoldenSpy has been packaged with a legitimate tax preparation software.

techniques.name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate hardware components in products prior to receipt by a final consumer for the purpose of data or system compromise.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to persistently execute code and perform various background tasks.

procedures.text: MarkiRAT can use BITS Utility to connect with the C2 server.
Patchwork has used BITS jobs to download malicious payloads.
Bazar has been downloaded via Windows BITS functionality.
Cobalt Strike can download a hosted "beacon" payload using BITSAdmin.

techniques.name: Trusted Relationship
techniques.summary: Adversaries may breach or otherwise leverage organizations who have access to intended victims.

procedures.text: GOLD SOUTHFIELD has breached Managed Service Providers (MSP's) to deliver malware to MSP customers.

NIMBUS MANTICORE has gained access to victim environments using trusted connections granted to third party partners, collaborators and contractors. NIMBUS MANTICORE has also leveraged trusted third-party services to include Citrix, VMwar...
Once APT28 gained access to the DCCC network, the group then proceeded to use that access to compromise the DNC network.
Threat Group-3390 has compromised third party service providers to gain access to victim's environments.

techniques.name: Hardware Additions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may physically introduce computer accessories, networking hardware, or other computing devices into a system or network that can be used as a vector to gain access.

procedures.text: DarkVishnya physically connected Bash Bunny, Raspberry Pi, netbooks, and inexpensive laptops to the target organization's environment to access the company’s local network.

techniques.name: Password Policy Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to access detailed information about the password policy used within an enterprise network or cloud environment.

procedures.text: The net accounts and net accounts /domain commands with Net can be used to obtain password policy information.
CrackMapExec can discover the password policies applied to the target system.
OilRig has used net.exe in a script with net accounts /domain to find the password policy of a domain.
Chimera has used the NtdsAudit utility to collect information related to accounts and passwords.

techniques.name: Indirect Command Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse utilities that allow for command execution to bypass security restrictions that limit the use of command-line interpreters.

procedures.text: Lazarus Group persistence mechanisms have used forfiles.exe to execute .htm files.
Forfiles can be used to subvert controls and possibly conceal command execution by not directly invoking cmd.
Revenge RAT uses the Forfiles utility to execute commands on the system.
RedCurl has used pcalua.exe to obfuscate binary execution and remote connections.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code. Vulnerabilities can exist in software due to unsecure coding practices that can lead to unanticipated behavior.

procedures.text: Sidewinder has exploited vulnerabilities to gain execution including CVE-2017-11882 and CVE-2020-0674.
Saint Bear has leveraged vulnerabilities in client applications such as CVE-2017-11882 in Microsoft Office to enable code execution in victim environments.
APT28 has exploited Microsoft Office vulnerability CVE-2017-0262 for execution.
Threat Group-3390 has exploited CVE-2018-0798 in Equation Editor.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.summary: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has impersonated organization IT and helpdesk staff to instruct victims to execute commercial remote access tools to gain initial access.

LAPSUS$ has recruited target organization employees or contractors who provide credentials and approve an associated MFA prompt, or install remote management software onto a corporate workstation, allowing LAPSUS$ to take control of an a...

Lumma Stealer has been distributed through a fake CAPTCHA that presents instructions to the victim to open Windows Run window (“Windows Button + R”) and paste clipboard contents (“CTRL + V”) and press “Enter” to execute a Base64-encoded...
Raspberry Robin execution can rely on users directly interacting with malicious LNK files.

techniques.name: Malicious Link
techniques.summary: An adversary may rely upon a user clicking a malicious link in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to click on a link that will lead to code execution.

procedures.text: FIN7 has used malicious links to lure victims into downloading malware.
BlackTech has used e-mails with malicious links to lure victims into installing malware.
Grandoreiro has used malicious links to gain execution on victim machines.
Bazar can gain execution after a user clicks on a malicious link to decoy landing pages hosted on Google Docs.

techniques.name: Malicious File
techniques.summary: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to open a file that will lead to code execution.

procedures.text: Malteiro has relied on users to execute .zip file attachments containing malicious URLs.
KOCTOPUS has relied on victims clicking a malicious document for execution.
KONNI has relied on a victim to enable malicious macros within an attachment delivered via email.
APT12 has attempted to get victims to open malicious Microsoft Word and PDF attachment sent via spearphishing.

techniques.name: Malicious Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may rely on a user running a malicious image to facilitate execution.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has relied on users to download and execute malicious Docker images.

techniques.name: Malicious Copy and Paste
techniques.summary: An adversary may rely upon a user copying and pasting code in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to copy and paste code directly into a Command and Scripting Interpreter.

procedures.text: Vidar has used fake CAPTCHAs to deliver and execute itself to victims.
MuddyWater has leveraged ClickFix type tactics enticing victims to copy and paste malicious PowerShell code.
Kimsuky has leveraged ClickFix type tactics enticing victims to copy and paste malicious code.
The Havoc infection chain has been initiated via ClickFix lures in phishing emails.

techniques.name: Malicious Library
techniques.summary: Adversaries may rely on a user installing a malicious library to facilitate execution. Threat actors may Upload Malware to package managers such as NPM and PyPi, as well as to public code repositories such as GitHub.

procedures.text: Contagious Interview has relied on users to install a malicious library from a code repository to infect the victim's device and has led to additional payload distribution and theft of sensitive data.

techniques.name: Traffic Signaling
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use traffic signaling to hide open ports or other malicious functionality used for persistence or command and control.

procedures.text: ZIPLINE can identify a specific string in intercepted network traffic, `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_0.3xx.`, to trigger its command functionality.
BUSHWALK can modify the `DSUserAgentCap.pm` Perl module on Ivanti Connect Secure VPNs and either activate or deactivate depending on the value of the user agent in incoming HTTP requests.
Penquin will connect to C2 only after sniffing a "magic packet" value in TCP or UDP packets matching specific conditions.
SYNful Knock can be sent instructions via special packets to change its functionality. Code for new functionality can be included in these messages.

techniques.name: Port Knocking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use port knocking to hide open ports used for persistence or command and control. To enable a port, an adversary sends a series of attempted connections to a predefined sequence of closed ports.

procedures.text: Mafalda can use port-knocking to authenticate itself to another implant called Cryshell to establish an indirect connection to the C2 server.
REPTILE has the ability to control compromised endpoints via port knocking.
PROMETHIUM has used a script that configures the knockd service and firewall to only accept C2 connections from systems that use a specified sequence of knock ports.
UNC3886 maintained persistence on FortiGate Firewalls through ICMP port knocking.

techniques.name: Socket Filters
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attach filters to a network socket to monitor then activate backdoors used for persistence or command and control.

procedures.text: CASTLETAP can listen for a specialized ICMP packet for activation on compromised network devices.

BPFDoor uses BPF bytecode to attach a filter to a network socket to view ICMP, UDP, or TCP packets coming through ports 22 (ssh), 80 (http), and 443 (https). When BPFDoor finds a packet containing its “magic” bytes, it parses out two fie...

PITSTOP can listen and evaluate incoming commands on the domain socket, created by PITHOOK malware, located at `/data/runtime/cockpit/wd.fd` for a predefined magic byte sequence. PITSTOP can then duplicate the socket for further communic...
Penquin installs a `TCP` and `UDP` filter on the `eth0` interface.

techniques.name: Rogue Domain Controller
techniques.summary: Adversaries may register a rogue Domain Controller to enable manipulation of Active Directory data. DCShadow may be used to create a rogue Domain Controller (DC).

procedures.text: Mimikatz’s LSADUMP::DCShadow module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems once inside of a network.

procedures.text: Flame can use MS10-061 to exploit a print spooler vulnerability in a remote system with a shared printer in order to move laterally.
WannaCry uses an exploit in SMBv1 to spread itself to other remote systems on a network.
Wizard Spider has exploited or attempted to exploit Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) and EternalBlue (MS17-010) vulnerabilities.
ShinyHunters has exploited vulnerabilities in remote services for lateral movement.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Stealth
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities to evade detection by hiding activity, suppressing logging, or operating within trusted or unmonitored components.

procedures.text: Velvet Ant exploited CVE-2024-20399 in Cisco Switches to which the threat actor was already able to authenticate in order to escape the NX-OS command line interface and gain access to the underlying operating system for arbitrary command...
APT28 has used CVE-2015-4902 to bypass security features.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to collect credentials.

procedures.text: UNC3886 exploited CVE-2022-22948 in VMware vCenter to obtain encrypted credentials from the vCenter postgresDB.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage information repositories to mine valuable information.

procedures.text: NIMBUS MANTICORE has gathered data from internal service ticketing systems to include credentials.
Raccoon Stealer gathers information from repositories associated with cryptocurrency wallets and the Telegram messaging service.
Troll Stealer gathers information from the Government Public Key Infrastructure (GPKI) folder, associated with South Korean government public key infrastructure, on infected systems.
APT28 has collected files from various information repositories.

techniques.name: Confluence
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage Confluence repositories to mine valuable information.

procedures.text: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for collaboration platforms like Confluence and JIRA to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
TruffleHog has collected credentials and data associated with Confluence.

techniques.name: Sharepoint
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage the SharePoint repository as a source to mine valuable information.

procedures.text: TruffleHog has searched SharePoint for data and credentials.
Akira has accessed and downloaded information stored in SharePoint instances as part of data gathering and exfiltration activity.
HAFNIUM has abused compromised credentials to exfiltrate data from SharePoint.
LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for collaboration platforms like SharePoint to discover further high-privilege account credentials.

techniques.name: Code Repositories
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage code repositories to collect valuable information. Code repositories are tools/services that store source code and automate software builds.

procedures.text: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for code repositories like GitLab and GitHub to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
GlassWorm has gathered code repository authentication materials for NPM and GitHub. GlassWorm has collected details pertaining to the npm configuration data for `_authToken`.
ShinyHunters has gathered information from and has searched for vulnerabilities in the target company’s GitHub repository source code.
Scattered Spider enumerates data stored within victim code repositories, such as internal GitHub repositories.

techniques.name: Customer Relationship Management Software
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software to mine valuable information.

techniques.name: Messaging Applications
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage chat and messaging applications, such as Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, and Slack, to mine valuable information.

procedures.text: TruffleHog has obtained data and credentials associated with messaging applications to include Slack.

APT38 has gathered Telegram Desktop messaging data from the applications data directories stored on the victim device to include cryptographic key material, and session mapping files that can recreate a compromised user’s Telegram sessio...
Fox Kitten has accessed victim security and IT environments and Microsoft Teams to mine valuable information.
Scattered Spider threat actors search the victim’s Slack and Microsoft Teams for conversations about the intrusion and incident response.

techniques.name: Databases
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage databases to mine valuable information. These databases may be hosted on-premises or in the cloud (both in platform-as-a-service and software-as-a-service environments).

procedures.text: GlassWorm has collected data from macOS devices through the gathering of Apple Notes related files by targeting `/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.notes/NoteStore.sqlite`, `/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.notes/NoteStor...
TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can extract credentials from multiple database configuration files including ~/.pgpass, ~/.my.cnf, ~/.mongorc.js, and /etc/mysql/my.cnf.
Sandworm Team exfiltrates data of interest from enterprise databases using Adminer.
APT38 has copied Apple Notes database from its application container and staged for upload.

techniques.name: System Script Proxy Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use trusted scripts, often signed with certificates, to proxy the execution of malicious files.

techniques.name: PubPrn
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use PubPrn to proxy execution of malicious remote files. PubPrn.vbs is a Visual Basic script that publishes a printer to Active Directory Domain Services.

procedures.text: APT32 has used PubPrn.vbs within execution scripts to execute malware, possibly bypassing defenses.

techniques.name: SyncAppvPublishingServer
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to proxy execution of malicious PowerShell commands.

techniques.name: Browser Information Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate information about browsers to learn more about compromised environments.

procedures.text: Calisto collects information on bookmarks from Google Chrome.
Lizar can retrieve browser history and database files.
Kimsuky has collected sensitive browser data using the function `GetBrowserData()` to include login credentials, bookmarks, cookies, and encryption keys.
Machete retrieves the user profile data (e.g., browsers) from Chrome and Firefox browsers.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed, or otherwise trusted, binaries.

procedures.text: Lazarus Group lnk files used for persistence have abused the Windows Update Client ( wuauclt.exe ) to execute a malicious DLL.
Volt Typhoon has used native tools and processes including living off the land binaries or “LOLBins" to maintain and expand access to the victim networks.

techniques.name: Compiled HTML File
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Compiled HTML files (.chm) to conceal malicious code. CHM files are commonly distributed as part of the Microsoft HTML Help system.

procedures.text: OilRig has used a CHM payload to load and execute another malicious file once delivered to a victim.
Dark Caracal leveraged a compiled HTML file that contained a command to download and run an executable.
Silence has weaponized CHM files in their phishing campaigns.
APT41 used compiled HTML (.chm) files for targeting.

techniques.name: Control Panel
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse control.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads.

procedures.text: InvisiMole can register itself for execution and persistence via the Control Panel.
Reaver drops and executes a malicious CPL file as its payload.

techniques.name: CMSTP
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse CMSTP to proxy execution of malicious code. The Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (CMSTP.exe) is a command-line program used to install Connection Manager service profiles.

procedures.text: CHIMNEYSWEEP can use CMSTP.exe to install a malicious Microsoft Connection Manager Profile.
MuddyWater has used CMSTP.exe and a malicious INF to execute its POWERSTATS payload.
LockBit 3.0 can attempt a CMSTP UAC bypass if it does not have administrative privileges.
Cobalt Group has used the command cmstp.exe /s /ns C:\Users\ADMINI~W\AppData\Local\Temp\XKNqbpzl.txt to bypass AppLocker and launch a malicious script.

techniques.name: InstallUtil
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use InstallUtil to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility.

procedures.text: Chaes has used Installutill to download content.
Mustang Panda has used InstallUtil.exe to execute a malicious Beacon stager.
WhisperGate has used `InstallUtil.exe` as part of its process to disable Windows Defender.
Covenant can create launchers via an InstallUtil XML file to install new Grunt listeners.

techniques.name: Mshta
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious .hta files and Javascript or VBScript through a trusted Windows utility.

procedures.text: Sidewinder has used mshta.exe to execute malicious payloads.
Lazarus Group has used mshta.exe to execute HTML pages downloaded by initial access documents.
Koadic can use mshta to serve additional payloads and to help schedule tasks for persistence.
MuddyWater has used mshta.exe to execute its POWERSTATS payload and to pass a PowerShell one-liner for execution.

techniques.name: Msiexec
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse msiexec.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Msiexec.exe is the command-line utility for the Windows Installer and is thus commonly associated with executing installation packages (.msi).

procedures.text: Chaes has used .MSI files as an initial way to start the infection chain.
Molerats has used msiexec.exe to execute an MSI payload.

Duqu has used msiexec to execute malicious Windows Installer packages. Additionally, a PROPERTY=VALUE pair containing a 56-bit encryption key has been used to decrypt the main payload from the installer packages.
Metamorfo has used MsiExec.exe to automatically execute files.

techniques.name: Odbcconf
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse odbcconf.exe to proxy execution of malicious payloads. Odbcconf.exe is a Windows utility that allows you to configure Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) drivers and data source names.

procedures.text: Cobalt Group has used odbcconf to proxy the execution of malicious DLL files.
Bumblebee can use `odbcconf.exe` to run DLLs on targeted hosts.

Raspberry Robin uses the Windows utility odbcconf.exe to execute malicious commands, using the regsvr flag to execute DLLs and bypass application control mechanisms that are not monitoring for odbcconf.exe abuse.

techniques.name: Regsvcs/Regasm
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Regsvcs and Regasm to proxy execution of code through a trusted Windows utility.

procedures.text: Agent Tesla has dropped RegAsm.exe onto systems for performing malicious activity.

techniques.name: Regsvr32
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

procedures.text: Saint Bot has used `regsvr32` to execute scripts.
QakBot can use Regsvr32 to execute malicious DLLs.
TA551 has used regsvr32.exe to load malicious DLLs.
Emotet uses RegSvr32 to execute the DLL payload.

techniques.name: Rundll32
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code. Using rundll32.exe, vice executing directly (i.e.

procedures.text: InvisiMole has used rundll32.exe for execution.
Latrodectus can use rundll32.exe to execute downloaded DLLs.
PUNCHBUGGY can load a DLL using Rundll32.
BoomBox can use RunDLL32 for execution.

techniques.name: Verclsid
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse verclsid.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

procedures.text: Hancitor has used verclsid.exe to download and execute a malicious script.

techniques.name: Mavinject
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse mavinject.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

procedures.text: TONESHELL has injected its malicious payload into a running process through Windows utility Microsoft Application Virtualization Injector `MAVInject.exe`.

techniques.name: MMC
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse mmc.exe to proxy execution of malicious .msc files.

procedures.text: Medusa Group has leveraged Microsoft Management Console (MMC) to facilitate lateral movement and to interact locally or remotely with victim devices using the command `mmc.exe compmgmt.msc /computer:{hostname/ip}`.

techniques.name: Electron Applications
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse components of the Electron framework to execute malicious code. The Electron framework hosts many common applications such as Signal, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

procedures.text: Lumma Stealer as leveraged Electron Applications to disable GPU sandboxing to avoid detection by security software.

techniques.name: Remote Access Tools
techniques.summary: An adversary may use legitimate remote access tools to establish an interactive command and control channel within a network.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has established tmate sessions for C2 communications.
Dridex contains a module for VNC.
RTM has the capability to download a VNC module from command and control (C2).
OilRig has incorporated remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools into their operations including ngrok.

techniques.name: IDE Tunneling
