techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Integrated Development Environment (IDE) software with remote development features to establish an interactive command and control channel on target systems within a network.

procedures.text: Mustang Panda has utilized an established Github account to create a tunnel within the victim environment using Visual Studio Code through the `code.exe tunnel` command.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop Software
techniques.summary: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support software to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.

procedures.text: Storm-0501 has used legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools including AnyDesk, NinjaOne, and Level.io.
Contagious Interview has downloaded remote management and monitoring software such as “AnyDesk” for post compromise activities.
EVILNUM has used the malware variant, TerraTV, to run a legitimate TeamViewer application to connect to compromised machines.
Storm-1811 has abused multiple types of legitimate remote access software and tools, such as ScreenConnect, NetSupport Manager, and AnyDesk.

techniques.name: Remote Access Hardware
techniques.summary: An adversary may use legitimate remote access hardware to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.

techniques.name: XSL Script Processing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bypass application control and obscure execution of code by embedding scripts inside XSL files.

procedures.text: Astaroth executes embedded JScript or VBScript in an XSL stylesheet located on a remote domain.
Cobalt Group used msxsl.exe to bypass AppLocker and to invoke Jscript code from an XSL file.
Higaisa used an XSL file to run VBScript code.

techniques.name: Template Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify references in user document templates to conceal malicious code or force authentication attempts.

procedures.text: Dragonfly has injected SMB URLs into malicious Word spearphishing attachments to initiate Forced Authentication.
Confucius has used a weaponized Microsoft Word document with an embedded RTF exploit.
Tropic Trooper delivered malicious documents with the XLSX extension, typically used by OpenXML documents, but the file itself was actually an OLE (XLS) document.
APT28 used weaponized Microsoft Word documents abusing the remote template function to retrieve a malicious macro.

techniques.name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files.

procedures.text: Qilin can use symbolic links to redirect file paths for remote and local objects and can use `chmod +x` to make its payload binary executable.

techniques.name: Windows Permissions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files.

procedures.text: JPIN can use the command-line utility cacls.exe to change file permissions.

The Gentlemen Ransomware has modified the ownership and access control settings to ensure it has unrestricted write access to target file paths prior to encryption. The Gentlemen Ransomware has leveraged the `takeown`, `icacls` and `attr...
Diskpart can be used to display, set, or clear attributes of a disk or volume.
BitPaymer can use icacls /reset and takeown /F to reset a targeted executable's permissions and then take ownership.

techniques.name: Linux and Mac Permissions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify file or directory permissions/attributes to evade access control lists (ACLs) and access protected files.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has modified the permissions on binaries with chattr .
OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D has changed permissions of a second-stage payload to an executable via chmod .
DRYHOOK has the ability to remount the filesystem as “read-write” to make changes and then restores it to “read-only” prior to killing processes to apply the modifications.
P.A.S. Webshell has the ability to modify file permissions.

techniques.name: Execution Guardrails
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use execution guardrails to constrain execution or actions based on adversary supplied and environment specific conditions that are expected to be present on the target.

procedures.text: DEADEYE can ensure it executes only on intended systems by identifying the victim's volume serial number, hostname, and/or DNS domain.
If a debugger or analysis environment is detected, Vidar has triggered a memory access violation exception, terminating its process by calling `RtlExitUserProcess`.
Exbyte checks for the presence of a configuration file before completing execution.
CHIMNEYSWEEP can execute a task which leads to execution if it finds a process name containing “creensaver.”

techniques.name: Environmental Keying
techniques.summary: Adversaries may environmentally key payloads or other features of malware to evade defenses and constraint execution to a specific target environment.

procedures.text: TONESHELL has generated unique GUIDs to identify victim devices. TONESHELL has leveraged environmental keying in payload delivery using the victim computer name and other configuration values. TONESHELL has also tracked IDs associated wi...
Equation has been observed utilizing environmental keying in payload delivery.

APT41 has encrypted payloads using the Data Protection API (DPAPI), which relies on keys tied to specific user accounts on specific machines. APT41 has also environmentally keyed second stage malware with an RC5 key derived in part from...
ROKRAT relies on a specific victim hostname to execute and decrypt important strings.

techniques.name: Mutual Exclusion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may constrain execution or actions based on the presence of a mutex associated with malware. A mutex is a locking mechanism used to synchronize access to a resource.

procedures.text: Embargo has utilized a hardcoded mutex name of “LoadUpOnGunsBringYourFriends” using the `CreateMutexW()` function. Embargo has also utilized a hardcoded mutex name of “IntoTheFloodAgainSameOldTrip."
Qilin can create a mutex to ensure only one instance is running.
PureCrypter code contains a global mutex.
When executed, BPFDoor attempts to create and lock a runtime file, `/var/run/initd.lock`, and exits if it fails using the specified file, resulting in a makeshift mutex.

techniques.name: Domain Trust Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gather information on domain trust relationships that may be used to identify lateral movement opportunities in Windows multi-domain/forest environments.

procedures.text: Empire has modules for enumerating domain trusts.
BlackByte enumerated Active Directory information and trust relationships during operations.
Bazar can use Nltest tools to obtain information about the domain.
IcedID used Nltest during initial discovery.

techniques.name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the configuration settings of a domain or identity tenant to evade defenses and/or escalate privileges in centrally managed environments.

techniques.name: Group Policy Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to subvert the intended discretionary access controls for a domain, usually with the intention of escalating privileges on the domain.

procedures.text: Prestige has been deployed using the Default Domain Group Policy Object from an Active Directory Domain Controller.
LockBit 3.0 can enable options for propogation through Group Policy Objects.
VOID MANTICORE had utilized Group Policy logon scripts to distribute the malicious payloads to victim devices through the execution of a batch file.
Storm-0501 distributed Group Policy Objects to tamper with security products.

techniques.name: Trust Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may add new domain trusts, modify the properties of existing domain trusts, or otherwise change the configuration of trust relationships between domains and tenants to evade defenses and/or elevate privile...

procedures.text: Scattered Spider adds a federated identity provider to the victim’s SSO tenant and activates automatic account linking.
AADInternals can create a backdoor by converting a domain to a federated domain which will be able to authenticate any user across the tenant. AADInternals can also modify DesktopSSO information.
Storm-0501 created a new federated domain within the victim Microsoft Entra tenant using Global Administrator level access to establish a persistent backdoor for later use.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.summary: Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources.

procedures.text: Diavol can delete specified files from a targeted system.
WhisperGate can corrupt files by overwriting the first 1 MB with `0xcc` and appending random extensions.
Industroyer’s data wiper module clears registry keys and overwrites both ICS configuration and Windows files.
LAPSUS$ has deleted the target's systems and resources both on-premises and in the cloud.

techniques.name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the lifecycle policies of a cloud storage bucket to destroy all objects stored within.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.summary: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources.

procedures.text: Maze has disrupted systems by encrypting files on targeted machines, claiming to decrypt files if a ransom payment is made. Maze has used the ChaCha algorithm, based on Salsa20, and an RSA algorithm to encrypt files.
Bad Rabbit has encrypted files and disks using AES-128-CBC and RSA-2048.
ThiefQuest encrypts a set of file extensions on a host, deletes the original files, and provides a ransom note with no contact information.
APT38 has used Hermes ransomware to encrypt files with AES256.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users.

procedures.text: Clop can kill several processes and services related to backups and security solutions.
Medusa Group has terminated services related to backups, security, databases, communication, filesharing and websites.
LookBack can kill processes and delete services.

Embargo has terminated active processes and services based on a hardcoded list using the `CloseServiceHandle()` function. Embargo has also leveraged MS4Killer to terminate processes contained in an embedded list of security software proc...

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.

procedures.text: Medusa Group has deleted recovery files such as shadow copies using `vssadmin.exe`.
Black Basta can delete shadow copies using vssadmin.exe.
Ragnar Locker can delete volume shadow copies using vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet .
InvisiMole can can remove all system restore points.

techniques.name: Defacement
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify visual content available internally or externally to an enterprise network, thus affecting the integrity of the original content.

techniques.name: Internal Defacement
techniques.summary: An adversary may deface systems internal to an organization in an attempt to intimidate or mislead users, thus discrediting the integrity of the systems.

procedures.text: Remcos has the ability to modify the desktop wallpaper.
Gamaredon Group has left taunting images and messages on the victims' desktops as proof of system access.
ShrinkLocker renames disk labels on victim hosts to the threat actor's email address to enable the victim to contact the threat actor for ransom negotiation.
Black Basta has set the desktop wallpaper on victims' machines to display a ransom note.

techniques.name: External Defacement
techniques.summary: An adversary may deface systems external to an organization in an attempt to deliver messaging, intimidate, or otherwise mislead an organization or users.

procedures.text: Ember Bear is linked to the defacement of several Ukrainian organization websites.
Sandworm Team defaced approximately 15,000 websites belonging to Georgian government, non-government, and private sector organizations in 2019.

techniques.name: Firmware Corruption
techniques.summary: Adversaries may overwrite or corrupt the flash memory contents of system BIOS or other firmware in devices attached to a system in order to render them inoperable or unable to boot, thus denying the availability to us...

procedures.text: Bad Rabbit has used an executable that installs a modified bootloader to prevent normal boot-up.
TrickBot module "Trickboot" can write or erase the UEFI/BIOS firmware of a compromised device.

techniques.name: Resource Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage the resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

techniques.name: Compute Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage the compute resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

procedures.text: Lucifer can use system resources to mine cryptocurrency, dropping XMRig to mine Monero.
Skidmap is a kernel-mode rootkit used for cryptocurrency mining.
CookieMiner has loaded coinmining software onto systems to mine for Koto cryptocurrency.
Rocke has distributed cryptomining malware.

techniques.name: Bandwidth Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage the network bandwidth resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

techniques.name: SMS Pumping
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage messaging services for SMS pumping, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

techniques.name: Cloud Service Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage compromised software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact hosted service availability.

techniques.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

procedures.text: StoneDrill has used several anti-emulation techniques to prevent automated analysis by emulators or sandboxes.
IcedID has manipulated Keitaro Traffic Direction System to filter researcher and sandbox traffic.
Agent Tesla has the ability to perform anti-sandboxing and anti-virtualization checks.
Contagious Interview has requested victims to disable Docker and other container environments in attempts to thwart container isolation and ensure device infection.

techniques.name: System Checks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various system checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

procedures.text: QakBot can check the compromised host for the presence of multiple executables associated with analysis tools and halt execution if any are found.
Denis ran multiple system checks, looking for processor and register characteristics, to evade emulation and analysis.
SodaMaster can check for the presence of the Registry key HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\\Applications\\VMwareHostOpen.exe before proceeding to its main functionality.
Okrum's loader can check the amount of physical memory and terminates itself if the host has less than 1.5 Gigabytes of physical memory in total.

techniques.name: User Activity Based Checks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various user activity checks to detect and avoid virtualization and analysis environments.

procedures.text: Darkhotel has used malware that repeatedly checks the mouse cursor position to determine if a real user is on the system.
Okrum loader only executes the payload after the left mouse button has been pressed at least three times, in order to avoid being executed within virtualized or emulated environments.
TONESHELL has leveraged `GetForegroundWindow` to detect virtualization or sandboxes by calling the API twice and comparing each window handle.
FIN7 used images embedded into document lures that only activate the payload when a user double clicks to avoid sandboxes.

techniques.name: Time Based Checks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various time-based methods to detect virtualization and analysis environments, particularly those that attempt to manipulate time mechanisms to simulate longer elapses of time.

procedures.text: After initial installation, Raindrop runs a computation to delay execution.
P8RAT has the ability to "sleep" for a specified time to evade detection.
SUNBURST remained dormant after initial access for a period of up to two weeks.
BendyBear can check for analysis environments and signs of debugging using the Windows API kernel32!GetTickCountKernel32 call.

techniques.name: Network Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users.

procedures.text: In 2016, APT28 conducted a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack against the World Anti-Doping Agency.
NKAbuse enables multiple types of network denial of service capabilities across several protocols post-installation.
Lucifer can execute TCP, UDP, and HTTP denial of service (DoS) attacks.

techniques.name: Direct Network Flood
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by directly sending a high-volume of network traffic to a target.

techniques.name: Reflection Amplification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by reflecting a high-volume of network traffic to a target.

techniques.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users.

procedures.text: OnionDuke has the capability to use a Denial of Service module.
Sandworm Team temporarily disrupted service to Georgian government, non-government, and private sector websites after compromising a Georgian web hosting provider in 2019.
ZxShell has a feature to perform SYN flood attack on a host.

techniques.name: OS Exhaustion Flood
techniques.summary: Adversaries may launch a denial of service (DoS) attack targeting an endpoint's operating system (OS).

techniques.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target the different network services provided by systems to conduct a denial of service (DoS).

techniques.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target resource intensive features of applications to cause a denial of service (DoS), denying availability to those applications.

techniques.name: Application or System Exploitation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities that can cause an application or system to crash and deny availability to users.

procedures.text: Industroyer uses a custom DoS tool that leverages CVE-2015-5374 and targets hardcoded IP addresses of Siemens SIPROTEC devices.

techniques.name: Server Software Component
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse legitimate extensible development features of servers to establish persistent access to systems.

techniques.name: SQL Stored Procedures
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse SQL stored procedures to establish persistent access to systems.

procedures.text: Stuxnet used xp_cmdshell to store and execute SQL code.

techniques.name: Transport Agent
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Microsoft transport agents to establish persistent access to systems.

procedures.text: LightNeuron has used a malicious Microsoft Exchange transport agent for persistence.

techniques.name: Web Shell
techniques.summary: Adversaries may backdoor web servers with web shells to establish persistent access to systems.

procedures.text: CURIUM has been linked to web shells following likely server compromise as an initial access vector into victim networks.
P.A.S. Webshell can gain remote access and execution on target web servers.
OwaAuth is a Web shell that appears to be exclusively used by Threat Group-3390. It is installed as an ISAPI filter on Exchange servers and shares characteristics with the China Chopper Web shell.
Dragonfly has commonly created Web shells on victims' publicly accessible email and web servers, which they used to maintain access to a victim network and download additional malicious files.

techniques.name: IIS Components
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install malicious components that run on Internet Information Services (IIS) web servers to establish persistence.

procedures.text: RGDoor establishes persistence on webservers as an IIS module.
IceApple is an IIS post-exploitation framework, consisting of 18 modules that provide several functionalities.
OwaAuth has been loaded onto Exchange servers and disguised as an ISAPI filter (owaauth.dll). The IIS w3wp.exe process then loads the malicious DLL.

techniques.name: Terminal Services DLL
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse components of Terminal Services to enable persistent access to systems.

techniques.name: vSphere Installation Bundles
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) to establish persistent access to ESXi hypervisors.

procedures.text: UNC3886 has used vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) to install malware and establish persistence across ESXi hypervisors.
VIRTUALPIE has been installed on VMware ESXi servers through malicious vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs).

techniques.name: Software Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of software and software versions that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment.

procedures.text: Metamorfo has searched the compromised system for banking applications.
XCSSET uses ps aux with the grep command to enumerate common browsers and system processes potentially impacting XCSSET's exfiltration capabilities.
Siloscape searches for the kubectl binary.
Volt Typhoon has queried the Registry on compromised systems for information on installed software.

techniques.name: Security Software Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of security software, configurations, defensive tools, and sensors that are installed on a system or in a cloud environment.

procedures.text: Darkhotel has searched for anti-malware strings and anti-virus processes running on the system.
Raspberry Robin attempts to identify security software running on the victim machine, such as BitDefender, Avast, and Kaspersky.
Clop can search for processes with antivirus and antimalware product names.
ABK has the ability to identify the installed anti-virus product on the compromised host.

techniques.name: Backup Software Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of backup software or configurations that are installed on a system.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has utilized the PowerShell script `Get-DataInfo.ps1` to collect installed backup software information from a compromised machine.

techniques.name: Implant Internal Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may implant cloud or container images with malicious code to establish persistence after gaining access to an environment.

techniques.name: Cloud Service Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to enumerate the cloud services running on a system after gaining access.

procedures.text: AADInternals can enumerate information about a variety of cloud services, such as Office 365 and Sharepoint instances or OpenID Configurations.
ROADTools can enumerate Azure AD applications and service principals.
Storm-0501 has discovered the victim environment’s protections to include Azure policies, resource locks, and Azure Storage immutability policies.
TruffleHog has the ability to scan code repositories and CI/CD platforms.

techniques.name: Steal Application Access Token
techniques.summary: Adversaries can steal application access tokens as a means of acquiring credentials to access remote systems and resources.

procedures.text: TeamPCP has used malware to steal access tokens from targeted cloud and developer environments.
CanisterWorm has gathered cloud access tokens.
Mini Shai-Hulud has stolen application access tokens and other tokens to include those associated with CI/CD.
APT29 uses stolen tokens to access victim accounts, without needing a password.

techniques.name: System Shutdown/Reboot
techniques.summary: Adversaries may shutdown/reboot systems to interrupt access to, or aid in the destruction of, those systems. Operating systems may contain commands to initiate a shutdown/reboot of a machine or network device.

procedures.text: AcidRain reboots the target system once the various wiping processes are complete.
DCSrv has a function to sleep for two hours before rebooting the system.
DynoWiper has used the Microsoft Windows native `ExitWindowsEx()` function to log off the interactive user and shutdown the system.
BFG Agonizer uses elevated privileges to call NtRaiseHardError to induce a "blue screen of death" on infected systems, causing a system crash. Once shut down, the system is no longer bootable.

techniques.name: Data from Cloud Storage
techniques.summary: Adversaries may access data from cloud storage. Many IaaS providers offer solutions for online data object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Storage, and Google Cloud Storage.

procedures.text: Fox Kitten has obtained files from the victim's cloud storage instances.
Peirates can dump the contents of AWS S3 buckets. It can also retrieve service account tokens from kOps buckets in Google Cloud Storage or S3.
Storm-0501 had modified Azure Storage account resources through the `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write` operation to expose non-remotely accessible accounts for data exfiltration.
APT42 has collected data from Microsoft 365 environments.

techniques.name: Account Access Removal
techniques.summary: Adversaries may interrupt availability of system and network resources by inhibiting access to accounts utilized by legitimate users.

procedures.text: Akira deletes administrator accounts in victim networks prior to encryption.
MegaCortex has changed user account passwords and logged users off the system.
LockerGoga has been observed changing account passwords and logging off current users.
Meteor has the ability to change the password of local users on compromised hosts and can log off users.

techniques.name: Internal Spearphishing
techniques.summary: After they already have access to accounts or systems within the environment, adversaries may use internal spearphishing to gain access to additional information or compromise other users within the same organization.

procedures.text: Gamaredon Group has used an Outlook VBA module on infected systems to send phishing emails with malicious attachments to other employees within the organization.
MuddyWater has used compromised mailboxes within target organizations to send spearphishing emails.
Kimsuky has sent internal spearphishing emails for lateral movement after stealing victim information.
SameCoin can send its Setup.exe file as an attachment to other addresses in the same compromised organization.

techniques.name: Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create cloud instances in unused geographic service regions in order to evade detection. Access is usually obtained through compromising accounts used to manage cloud infrastructure.

techniques.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exfiltrate data by transferring the data, including through sharing/syncing and creating backups of cloud environments, to another cloud account they control on the same service.

procedures.text: Storm-0501 has copied data from the victims environment to their own infrastructure leveraging AzCopy CLI.
INC Ransom has used Megasync to exfiltrate data to the cloud.
RedCurl has used cloud storage to exfiltrate data, in particular the megatools utilities were used to exfiltrate data to Mega, a file storage service.

techniques.name: Cloud Service Dashboard
techniques.summary: An adversary may use a cloud service dashboard GUI with stolen credentials to gain useful information from an operational cloud environment, such as specific services, resources, and features.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider abused AWS Systems Manager Inventory to identify targets on the compromised network prior to lateral movement.

techniques.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
techniques.summary: An adversary may steal web application or service session cookies and use them to gain access to web applications or Internet services as an authenticated user without needing credentials.

procedures.text: LuminousMoth has used an unnamed post-exploitation tool to steal cookies from the Chrome browser.
Kimsuky has used malware, such as TRANSLATEXT, to steal and exfiltrate browser cookies.
Sandworm Team used information stealer malware to collect browser session cookies.
Grandoreiro can steal the victim's cookies to use for duplicating the active session from another device.

techniques.name: Pre-OS Boot
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Pre-OS Boot mechanisms as a way to establish persistence on a system. During the booting process of a computer, firmware and various startup services are loaded before the operating system.

techniques.name: System Firmware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify system firmware to persist on systems.The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and The Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) or Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI) are examples of system firm...

procedures.text: LoJax is a UEFI BIOS rootkit deployed to persist remote access software on some targeted systems.
Trojan.Mebromi performs BIOS modification and can download and execute a file as well as protect itself from removal.
Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit is a UEFI BIOS rootkit developed by the company Hacking Team to persist remote access software on some targeted systems.

techniques.name: Component Firmware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify component firmware to persist on systems.

procedures.text: Equation is known to have the capability to overwrite the firmware on hard drives from some manufacturers.
Cyclops Blink has maintained persistence by patching legitimate device firmware when it is downloaded, including that of WatchGuard devices.

techniques.name: Bootkit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use bootkits to persist on systems. A bootkit is a malware variant that modifies the boot sectors of a hard drive, allowing malicious code to execute before a computer's operating system has loaded.

procedures.text: Carberp has installed a bootkit on the system to maintain persistence.
WhisperGate overwrites the MBR with a bootloader component that performs destructive wiping operations on hard drives and displays a fake ransom note when the host boots.
TrickBot can implant malicious code into a compromised device's firmware.
ROCKBOOT is a Master Boot Record (MBR) bootkit that uses the MBR to establish persistence.

techniques.name: ROMMONkit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse the ROM Monitor (ROMMON) by loading an unauthorized firmware with adversary code to provide persistent access and manipulate device behavior that is difficult to detect.

techniques.name: TFTP Boot
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse netbooting to load an unauthorized network device operating system from a Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify system-level processes to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

procedures.text: IMAPLoader modifies Windows tasks on the victim machine to reference a retrieved PE file through a path modification.
Akira _v2 can create a child process for encryption.
BOLDMOVE can free all resources and terminate itself on victim machines.
Exaramel for Linux has a hardcoded location that it uses to achieve persistence if the startup system is Upstart or System V and it is running as root.

techniques.name: Launch Agent
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify launch agents to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

procedures.text: Calisto adds a .plist file to the /Library/LaunchAgents folder to maintain persistence.
Mini Shai-Hulud has established persistence on macOS hosts by installing a gh-token-monitor daemon through LaunchAgent that polls GitHub every 60 seconds.
Proton persists via Launch Agent.
GlassWorm has established persistence on macOS via a LaunchAgent by writing a plist under `/library/LaunchAgents`.

techniques.name: Systemd Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify systemd services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

procedures.text: TeamPCP has used the systemd user service for malware persistence in targeted environments.
Shai-Hulud has stopped `systemd-resolved` in order to manipulate DNS and firewalls.
TeamTNT has established persistence through the creation of a cryptocurrency mining system service using systemctl .
Gomir creates a systemd service named `syslogd` for persistence.

techniques.name: Windows Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify Windows services to repeatedly execute malicious payloads as part of persistence.

procedures.text: NightClub has created a Windows service named `WmdmPmSp` to establish persistence.
Industroyer can use an arbitrary system service to load at system boot for persistence and replaces the ImagePath registry value of a Windows service with a new backdoor binary.
Tropic Trooper has installed a service pointing to a malicious DLL dropped to disk.
Medusa Group has used vulnerable or signed drivers to modify security solutions on victim devices.

techniques.name: Launch Daemon
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify Launch Daemons to execute malicious payloads as part of persistence. Launch Daemons are plist files used to interact with Launchd, the service management framework used by macOS.

procedures.text: The REPTILE launcher can daemonize a process.
Green Lambert can add a plist file in the `Library/LaunchDaemons` to establish persistence.
COATHANGER will create a daemon for timed check-ins with command and control infrastructure.

When running with root privileges after a Launch Agent is installed, ThiefQuest installs a plist file to the /Library/LaunchDaemons/ folder with the RunAtLoad key set to true establishing persistence as a Launch Daemon.

techniques.name: Container Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify container or container cluster management tools that run as daemons, agents, or services on individual hosts.

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has modified container service configurations using `Guest Shell`.

techniques.name: Event Triggered Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges using system mechanisms that trigger execution based on specific events.

procedures.text: Pacu can set up S3 bucket notifications to trigger a malicious Lambda function when a CloudFormation template is uploaded to the bucket. It can also create Lambda functions that trigger upon the creation of users, roles, and groups.
UPSTYLE creates a `.pth` file beginning with the text `import` so that any time another process or script attempts to reference the modified item the malicious code will also run.

XCSSET's `dfhsebxzod` module searches for `.xcodeproj` directories within the user’s home folder and subdirectories. For each match, it locates the corresponding `project.pbxproj` file and embeds an encoded payload into a build rule, tar...

Mini Shai-Hulud has modified settings and configuration files of AI coding agents and other coding applications in order to create event triggered executions through creating hooks and runOn conditions.

techniques.name: Change Default File Association
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by a file type association.

procedures.text: SILENTTRINITY can conduct an image hijack of an `.msc` file extension as part of its UAC bypass process.
Kimsuky has a HWP document stealer module which changes the default program association in the registry to open HWP documents.

techniques.name: Screensaver
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.

procedures.text: Gazer can establish persistence through the system screensaver by configuring it to execute the malware.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by a Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscription.

procedures.text: Blue Mockingbird has used mofcomp.exe to establish WMI Event Subscription persistence mechanisms configured from a *.mof file.
Sardonic can use a WMI event filter to invoke a command-line event consumer to gain persistence.
APT29 has used WMI event subscriptions for persistence.
metaMain registered a WMI event subscription consumer called "hard_disk_stat" to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence through executing malicious commands triggered by a user’s shell. User Unix Shells execute several configuration scripts at different points throughout the session based on events.

procedures.text: When executing with non-root level permissions, RotaJakiro can install persistence by adding a command to the .bashrc file that executes a binary in the `${HOME}/.gvfsd/.profile/` folder.
Linux Rabbit maintains persistence on an infected machine through rc.local and .bashrc files.
Contagious Interview has targeted macOS victim hosts using a bash downloader `coremedia.sh` and a bash script `cloud.sh`.
Green Lambert can establish persistence on a compromised host through modifying the `profile`, `login`, and run command (rc) files associated with the `bash`, `csh`, and `tcsh` shells.

techniques.name: Trap
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by an interrupt signal.

techniques.name: LC_LOAD_DYLIB Addition
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by the execution of tainted binaries.

techniques.name: Netsh Helper DLL
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by Netsh Helper DLLs.

procedures.text: netsh can be used as a persistence proxy technique to execute a helper DLL when netsh.exe is executed.

techniques.name: Accessibility Features
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by accessibility features.

procedures.text: Empire can leverage WMI debugging to remotely replace binaries like sethc.exe, Utilman.exe, and Magnify.exe with cmd.exe.
APT41 leveraged sticky keys to establish persistence.
APT3 replaces the Sticky Keys binary C:\Windows\System32\sethc.exe for persistence.
Deep Panda has used the sticky-keys technique to bypass the RDP login screen on remote systems during intrusions.

techniques.name: AppCert DLLs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppCert DLLs loaded into processes.

procedures.text: PUNCHBUGGY can establish using a AppCertDLLs Registry key.

techniques.name: AppInit DLLs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by AppInit DLLs loaded into processes.

procedures.text: APT39 has used malware to set LoadAppInit_DLLs in the Registry key SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows in order to establish persistence.

If a victim meets certain criteria, T9000 uses the AppInit_DLL functionality to achieve persistence by ensuring that every user mode process that is spawned will load its malicious DLL, ResN32.dll. It does this by creating the following...

Some variants of Cherry Picker use AppInit_DLLs to achieve persistence by creating the following Registry key: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows "AppInit_DLLs"="pserver32.dll"
Ramsay can insert itself into the address space of other applications using the AppInit DLL Registry key.

techniques.name: Application Shimming
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by application shims.

procedures.text: Pillowmint has used a malicious shim database to maintain persistence.
SDBbot has the ability to use application shimming for persistence if it detects it is running as admin on Windows XP or 7, by creating a shim database to patch services.exe.
FIN7 has used application shim databases for persistence.
ShimRat has installed shim databases in the AppPatch folder.

techniques.name: Image File Execution Options Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and/or elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by Image File Execution Options (IFEO) debuggers.

procedures.text: SUNBURST created an Image File Execution Options (IFEO) Debugger registry value for the process dllhost.exe to trigger the installation of Cobalt Strike.
SDBbot has the ability to use image file execution options for persistence if it detects it is running with admin privileges on a Windows version newer than Windows 7.

techniques.name: PowerShell Profile
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by PowerShell profiles.

procedures.text: Turla has used PowerShell profiles to maintain persistence on an infected machine.

techniques.name: Emond
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain persistence and elevate privileges by executing malicious content triggered by the Event Monitor Daemon (emond).

techniques.name: Component Object Model Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by hijacked references to Component Object Model (COM) objects.

procedures.text: Some variants of ADVSTORESHELL achieve persistence by registering the payload as a Shell Icon Overlay handler COM object.
KONNI has modified ComSysApp service to load the malicious DLL payload.
APT28 has used COM hijacking for persistence by replacing the legitimate MMDeviceEnumerator object with a payload.
PcShare has created the `HKCU\\Software\\Classes\\CLSID\\{42aedc87-2188-41fd-b9a3-0c966feabec1}\\InprocServer32` Registry key for persistence.

techniques.name: Installer Packages
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish persistence and elevate privileges by using an installer to trigger the execution of malicious content.

procedures.text: During AppleJeus's installation process, it uses `postinstall` scripts to extract a hidden plist from the application's `/Resources` folder and execute the `plist` file as a Launch Daemon with elevated permissions.
TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can inject malicious pre or post-install scripts within package.json for payload execution.
TeamPCP has modified software packages with preinstall scripts to download and execute malicious payloads.
Shai-Hulud has inserted a new lifecycle hook to include `postinstall`. Shai-Hulud has also leveraged the NPM lifecycle hook `preinstall`.

techniques.name: Udev Rules
techniques.summary: Adversaries may maintain persistence through executing malicious content triggered using udev rules.

procedures.text: REPTILE has used udev for persistence.

techniques.name: Python Startup Hooks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by leveraging Python’s startup mechanisms, including path configuration (`.pth`) files and the `sitecustomize.py` or `usercustomize.py` modules.

procedures.text: TeamPCP Cloud Stealer has used .pth files to establish persistence on compromised hosts due to the Python interpreter's automatic processing of .pth files at startup.
Mini Shai-Hulud has utilized Python startup hooks to include the .pth import mechanism for execution.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon to maintain persistence or gain higher-level privileges on compromised systems.

procedures.text: xCaon has added persistence via the Registry key HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\load which causes the malware to run each time any user logs in.
Dtrack’s RAT makes a persistent target file with auto execution on the host start.

Mis-Type has created registry keys for persistence, including `HKCU\Software\bkfouerioyou`, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{6afa8072-b2b1-31a8-b5c1-{Unique Identifier}`, and `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Set...
BoxCaon established persistence by setting the HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\load registry key to point to its executable.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to a startup folder or referencing it with a Registry run key.

procedures.text: Variants of Emissary have added Run Registry keys to establish persistence.
Pisloader establishes persistence via a Registry Run key.
EvilBunny has created Registry keys for persistence in [HKLM|HKCU]\…\CurrentVersion\Run .
An APT19 HTTP malware variant establishes persistence by setting the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Windows Debug Tools-%LOCALAPPDATA%\ .

techniques.name: Authentication Package
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse authentication packages to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows authentication package DLLs are loaded by the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start.

procedures.text: Flame can use Windows Authentication Packages for persistence.

techniques.name: Time Providers
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse time providers to execute DLLs when the system boots. The Windows Time service (W32Time) enables time synchronization across and within domains.

techniques.name: Winlogon Helper DLL
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse features of Winlogon to execute DLLs and/or executables when a user logs in.

procedures.text: Gazer can establish persistence by setting the value “Shell” with “explorer.exe, %malware_pathfile%” under the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon .
Qilin can configure a Winlogon registry entry.
DarkTortilla has established persistence via the `Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon` registry key.
A Dipsind variant registers as a Winlogon Event Notify DLL to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Security Support Provider
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse security support providers (SSPs) to execute DLLs when the system boots. Windows SSP DLLs are loaded into the Local Security Authority (LSA) process at system start.

procedures.text: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.
Empire can enumerate Security Support Providers (SSPs) as well as utilize PowerSploit's Install-SSP and Invoke-Mimikatz to install malicious SSPs and log authentication events.
PowerSploit's Install-SSP Persistence module can be used to establish by installing a SSP DLL.

techniques.name: Kernel Modules and Extensions
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the kernel to automatically execute programs on system boot. Loadable Kernel Modules (LKMs) are pieces of code that can be loaded and unloaded into the kernel upon demand.

procedures.text: Drovorub can use kernel modules to establish persistence.
Skidmap has the ability to install several loadable kernel modules (LKMs) on infected machines.
The REPTILE rootkit is implemented as a loadable kernel module (LKM).

techniques.name: Re-opened Applications
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify plist files to automatically run an application when a user logs in.

techniques.name: LSASS Driver
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify or add LSASS drivers to obtain persistence on compromised systems. The Windows security subsystem is a set of components that manage and enforce the security policy for a computer or domain.

procedures.text: Wingbird drops a malicious file (sspisrv.dll) alongside a copy of lsass.exe, which is used to register a service that loads sspisrv.dll as a driver. The payload of the malicious driver (located in its entry-point function) is executed wh...
Pasam establishes by infecting the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) DLL to load a malicious DLL dropped to disk.

techniques.name: Shortcut Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or modify shortcuts that can execute a program during system boot or user login.

procedures.text: RogueRobin establishes persistence by creating a shortcut (.LNK file) in the Windows startup folder to run a script each time the user logs in.
RedLeaves attempts to add a shortcut file in the Startup folder to achieve persistence.
Okrum can establish persistence by creating a .lnk shortcut to itself in the Startup folder.
Reaver creates a shortcut file and saves it in a Startup folder to establish persistence.

techniques.name: Port Monitors
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use port monitors to run an adversary supplied DLL during system boot for persistence or privilege escalation.

techniques.name: Print Processors
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse print processors to run malicious DLLs during system boot for persistence and/or privilege escalation.

procedures.text: Gelsemium can drop itself in C:\Windows\System32\spool\prtprocs\x64\winprint.dll to be loaded automatically by the spoolsv Windows service.
Earth Lusca has added the Registry key `HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Print\Environments\Windows x64\Print Processors\UDPrint” /v Driver /d “spool.dll /f` to load malware as a Print Processor.
The PipeMon installer has modified the Registry key HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Environments\Windows x64\Print Processors to install PipeMon as a Print Processor.

techniques.name: XDG Autostart Entries
techniques.summary: Adversaries may add or modify XDG Autostart Entries to execute malicious programs or commands when a user’s desktop environment is loaded at login.

procedures.text: NETWIRE can use XDG Autostart Entries to establish persistence on Linux systems.
Contagious Interview has established persistence using InvisibleFerret malware to create a .desktop entry to run on startup on GNOME-based Linux devices.
Pupy can use an XDG Autostart to establish persistence.
InvisibleFerret has established persistence within GNOME-based Linux environments by placing entries within `.desktop` that run on Startup.

techniques.name: Active Setup
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a Registry key to the Active Setup of the local machine. Active Setup is a Windows mechanism that is used to execute programs when a user logs in.

procedures.text: PoisonIvy creates a Registry key in the Active Setup pointing to a malicious executable.

techniques.name: Login Items
techniques.summary: Adversaries may add login items to execute upon user login to gain persistence or escalate privileges.

procedures.text: Green Lambert can add Login Items to establish persistence.
NETWIRE can persist via startup options for Login items.
Dok uses AppleScript to install a login Item by sending Apple events to the System Events process.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.summary: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control privilege elevation to gain higher-level permissions.

procedures.text: UNC3886 has used vSphere Installation Bundles (VIBs) that contained modified descriptor XML files with the `acceptance-level` set to `partner` which allowed for privilege escalation.
Raspberry Robin implements a variation of the ucmDccwCOMMethod technique abusing the Windows AutoElevate backdoor to bypass UAC while elevating privileges.

techniques.name: Setuid and Setgid
techniques.summary: An adversary may abuse configurations where an application has the setuid or setgid bits set in order to get code running in a different (and possibly more privileged) user’s context.

procedures.text: Keydnap adds the setuid flag to a binary so it can easily elevate in the future.
Exaramel for Linux can execute commands with high privileges via a specific binary with setuid functionality.

techniques.name: Bypass User Account Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bypass UAC mechanisms to elevate process privileges on system.

procedures.text: Vidar has bypassed UAC by setting the Registry value `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\EnableLUA` to `0`, which disabled UAC.
BlackEnergy attempts to bypass default User Access Control (UAC) settings by exploiting a backward-compatibility setting found in Windows 7 and later.
RTM can attempt to run the program as admin, then show a fake error message and a legitimate UAC bypass prompt to the user in an attempt to socially engineer the user into escalating privileges.
LockBit 3.0 can bypass UAC to execute code with elevated privileges through an elevated Component Object Model (COM) interface.

techniques.name: Sudo and Sudo Caching
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform sudo caching and/or use the sudoers file to elevate privileges. Adversaries may do this to execute commands as other users or spawn processes with higher privileges.

procedures.text: Cobalt Strike can use sudo to run a command.
Shai-Hulud has attempted to gain root access by leveraging `sudo` and `/etc/sudoers.d`.
TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can use `sudo` for code execution.
Salt Typhoon has elevated privileges of local user accounts by editing `/etc/sudoers` or adding a file under `/etc/sudoers.d/`.

techniques.name: Elevated Execution with Prompt
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API to escalate privileges by prompting the user for credentials.

procedures.text: OSX/Shlayer can escalate privileges to root by asking the user for credentials.

techniques.name: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse permission configurations that allow them to gain temporarily elevated access to cloud resources.

techniques.name: TCC Manipulation
techniques.summary: Adversaries can manipulate or abuse the Transparency, Consent, & Control (TCC) service or database to grant malicious executables elevated permissions.

procedures.text: For several modules, XCSSET attempts to access or list the contents of user folders such as Desktop, Downloads, and Documents. If the folder does not exist or access is denied, it enters a loop where it resets the TCC database and retrie...

APT38 has used Finder, a macOS native app with FDA permissions, to rename the folder `com.apple.TCC`, then used another process to move the `TCC.db` file to a new location, where SQLite3 was used to edit `TCC.db`. The edited `TCC.db` fil...

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use alternate authentication material, such as password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and application access tokens, in order to move laterally within an environment and bypass normal system access controls.

procedures.text: FoggyWeb can allow abuse of a compromised AD FS server's SAML token.

techniques.name: Application Access Token
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use stolen application access tokens to bypass the typical authentication process and access restricted accounts, information, or services on remote systems.

procedures.text: ShinyHunters has used stolen OAuth keys to access cloud infrastructure and to bypass two-factor authentication.
Peirates can use stolen service account tokens to perform its operations. It also enables adversaries to switch between valid service accounts.
TeamPCP has used stolen access tokens to inject malicious code into CI/CD workflows and to exfiltrate sensitive data from cloud, developer, and container environments.
CreepyDrive can use legitimate OAuth refresh tokens to authenticate with OneDrive.

techniques.name: Pass the Hash
techniques.summary: Adversaries may “pass the hash” using stolen password hashes to move laterally within an environment, bypassing normal system access controls.

procedures.text: APT32 has used pass the hash for lateral movement.
Cobalt Strike can perform pass the hash.
Pass-The-Hash Toolkit can perform pass the hash.
APT28 has used pass the hash for lateral movement.

techniques.name: Pass the Ticket
techniques.summary: Adversaries may “pass the ticket” using stolen Kerberos tickets to move laterally within an environment, bypassing normal system access controls.

procedures.text: Some SeaDuke samples have a module to use pass the ticket with Kerberos for authentication.
APT29 used Kerberos ticket attacks for lateral movement.
Mimikatz’s LSADUMP::DCSync and KERBEROS::PTT modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
Pupy can also perform pass-the-ticket.

techniques.name: Web Session Cookie
techniques.summary: Adversaries can use stolen session cookies to authenticate to web applications and services. This technique bypasses some multi-factor authentication protocols since the session is already authenticated.

procedures.text: Star Blizzard has bypassed multi-factor authentication on victim email accounts by using session cookies stolen using EvilGinx.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search compromised systems to find and obtain insecurely stored credentials. These credentials can be stored and/or misplaced in many locations on a system, including plaintext files (e.g.

procedures.text: DarkGate uses NirSoft tools to steal user credentials from the infected machine. NirSoft tools are executed via process hollowing in a newly-created instance of vbc.exe or regasm.exe.
Pacu can search for sensitive data: for example, in Code Build environment variables, EC2 user data, and Cloud Formation templates.
Astaroth uses an external software known as NetPass to recover passwords.
NIMBUS MANTICORE has obtained credentials from internal service ticketing systems.

techniques.name: Credentials In Files
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search local file systems and remote file shares for files containing insecurely stored credentials.

procedures.text: XTunnel is capable of accessing locally stored passwords on victims.
Pupy can use Lazagne for harvesting credentials.
Emotet has been observed leveraging a module that retrieves passwords stored on a system for the current logged-on user.
PoshC2 contains modules for searching for passwords in local and remote files.

techniques.name: Credentials in Registry
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search the Registry on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials. The Windows Registry stores configuration information that can be used by the system or other programs.

procedures.text: Reg may be used to find credentials in the Windows Registry.

PowerSploit has several modules that search the Windows Registry for stored credentials: Get-UnattendedInstallFile , Get-Webconfig , Get-ApplicationHost , Get-SiteListPassword , Get-CachedGPPPassword , and Get-RegistryAutoLogon .
APT32 used Outlook Credential Dumper to harvest credentials stored in Windows registry.
IceApple can harvest credentials from local and remote host registries.

techniques.name: Shell History
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search the command history on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.

procedures.text: Kinsing has searched bash_history for credentials.
TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can target credentials in shell history on self-hosted runners.
APT38 has gathered data and credentials stored in Shell History.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has extracted system data to include histories.

techniques.name: Private Keys
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credentials.

procedures.text: Machete has scanned and looked for cryptographic keys and certificate file extensions.
Mimikatz's CRYPTO::Extract module can extract keys by interacting with Windows cryptographic application programming interface (API) functions.
TeamPCP has used malware to extract SSH and GPG keys from victim environments.
Kinsing has searched for private keys.

techniques.name: Cloud Instance Metadata API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to access the Cloud Instance Metadata API to collect credentials and other sensitive data.

procedures.text: Mini Shai-Hulud has gathered credentials and secrets from AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Azure metadata API.
TeamTNT has queried the AWS instance metadata service for credentials.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has a module that is capable of gathering Cloud Instance Metadata to include AWS, Google Cloud Platform, and Azure.
TruffleHog can query the AWS and GCP metadata endpoints for instances and service credentials.

techniques.name: Group Policy Preferences
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to find unsecured credentials in Group Policy Preferences (GPP). GPP are tools that allow administrators to create domain policies with embedded credentials.

procedures.text: SILENTTRINITY has a module that can extract cached GPP passwords.
PowerSploit contains a collection of Exfiltration modules that can harvest credentials from Group Policy Preferences.
MirrorStealer can target Group Policy Preferences for credentials.
APT33 has used a variety of publicly available tools like Gpppassword to gather credentials.

techniques.name: Container API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather credentials via APIs within a containers environment.

procedures.text: TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can query the Kubernetes API for credentials.
Mini Shai-Hulud has gathered unsecured API keys stored in container orchestrators.
Peirates can query the Kubernetes API for secrets.

techniques.name: Chat Messages
techniques.summary: Adversaries may directly collect unsecured credentials stored or passed through user communication services.

procedures.text: LAPSUS$ has targeted various collaboration tools like Slack, Teams, JIRA, Confluence, and others to hunt for exposed credentials to support privilege escalation and lateral movement.

techniques.name: Subvert Trust Controls
techniques.summary: Adversaries may undermine security controls that will either warn users of untrusted activity or prevent execution of untrusted programs.

procedures.text: Axiom has used digital certificates to deliver malware.
Shai-Hulud has suppressed victim NPM warnings using `process“exit’;` which results in having all errors exit with code 0.

techniques.name: Gatekeeper Bypass
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify file attributes and subvert Gatekeeper functionality to evade user prompts and execute untrusted programs.

procedures.text: XCSSET has dropped a malicious applet into an app's `.../Contents/MacOS/` folder of a previously launched app to bypass Gatekeeper's security checks on first launch apps (prior to macOS 13).

If running with elevated privileges, OSX/Shlayer has used the spctl command to disable Gatekeeper protection for a downloaded file. OSX/Shlayer can also leverage system links pointing to bash scripts in the downloaded DMG file to bypass...
Cuckoo Stealer can use `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` to remove the quarantine flag attribute.
MacMa has removed the `com.apple.quarantineattribute` from the dropped file, `$TMPDIR/airportpaird`.

techniques.name: Code Signing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create, acquire, or steal code signing materials to sign their malware or tools.

procedures.text: Cobalt Strike can use self signed Java applets to execute signed applet attacks.
BackConfig has been signed with self signed digital certificates mimicking a legitimate software company.
RedLine Stealer has used both valid certificates and self-signed digital certificates to appear legitimate.

FIN7 has signed Carbanak payloads with legally purchased code signing certificates. FIN7 has also digitally signed their phishing documents, backdoors and other staging tools to bypass security controls.

techniques.name: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may tamper with SIP and trust provider components to mislead the operating system and application control tools when conducting signature validation checks.

techniques.name: Install Root Certificate
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.

procedures.text: certutil can be used to install browser root certificates as a precursor to performing Adversary-in-the-Middle between connections to banking websites. Example command: certutil -addstore -f -user ROOT ProgramData\cert512121.der .
Dok installs a root certificate to aid in Adversary-in-the-Middle actions using the command add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /tmp/filename .
Hikit installs a self-generated certificate to the local trust store as a root CA and Trusted Publisher.
evilginx2 has obtained a valid SSL/TLS certificate from LetsEncrypt to provide responses to Automatic Certificate Management Environment (ACME) challenges.

techniques.name: Mark-of-the-Web Bypass
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse specific file formats to subvert Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) controls.

procedures.text: TA505 has used .iso files to deploy malicious .lnk files.
Amadey has modified the `:Zone.Identifier` in the ADS area to zero.
APT38 has used ISO and VHD files to deploy malware and to bypass Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) security measures.
QakBot has been packaged in ISO files in order to bypass Mark of the Web (MOTW) security measures.

techniques.name: Code Signing Policy Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify code signing policies to enable execution of unsigned or self-signed code.

procedures.text: APT39 has used malware to turn off the RequireSigned feature which ensures only signed DLLs can be run on Windows.
BlackEnergy has enabled the TESTSIGNING boot configuration option to facilitate loading of a driver component.
Hikit has attempted to disable driver signing verification by tampering with several Registry keys prior to the loading of a rootkit driver component.
Pandora can use CVE-2017-15303 to disable Windows Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) protection and load its driver.

techniques.name: Compromise Host Software Binary
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify host software binaries to establish persistent access to systems. Software binaries/executables provide a wide range of system commands or services, programs, and libraries.

procedures.text: PHASEJAM has modified legitimate components to enable persistence and execution, including inserting a web shell into `getComponent.cgi` and `restAuth.cgi`, modifying `DSUpgrade.pm` to block system upgrades, and overwriting `remotedebug`...
Mini Shai-Hulud has established persistence through modifying software binaries to include AI coding agents’ configuration or setting files that act as hooks, tasks or execution triggers.
WARPWIRE can embed itself into a legitimate file on compromised Ivanti Connect Secure VPNs.
UNC3886 has trojanized Fortinet firmware and replaced the legitimate `/usr/bin/tac_plus` TACACS+ daemon for Linux with a malicious version containing credential logging functionality.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search for common password storage locations to obtain user credentials. Passwords are stored in several places on a system, depending on the operating system or application holding the credentials.

procedures.text: HEXANE has run `cmdkey` on victim machines to identify stored credentials.
MirrorStealer has the ability to steal credentials from email clients.
Carberp's passw.plug plugin can gather account information from multiple instant messaging, email, and social media services, as well as FTP, VNC, and VPN clients.

Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many w...

techniques.name: Keychain
techniques.summary: Adversaries may acquire credentials from Keychain.

procedures.text: Contagious Interview has leveraged malware variants configured to dump credentials from the macOS keychain.
LightSpy performs an in-memory keychain query via `SecItemCopyMatching()` then formats the retrieved data as a JSON blob for exfiltration.
GlassWorm has collected keys stored within `/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`.
Green Lambert can use Keychain Services API functions to find and collect passwords, such as `SecKeychainFindInternetPassword` and `SecKeychainItemCopyAttributesAndData`.

techniques.name: Securityd Memory
techniques.summary: An adversary with root access may gather credentials by reading `securityd`’s memory. `securityd` is a service/daemon responsible for implementing security protocols such as encryption and authorization.

procedures.text: Keydnap uses the keychaindump project to read securityd memory.

techniques.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
techniques.summary: Adversaries may acquire credentials from web browsers by reading files specific to the target browser.

procedures.text: njRAT has a module that steals passwords saved in victim web browsers.

BeaverTail has stolen passwords saved in web browsers. BeaverTail has also been known to collect login data from Firefox within key3.db, key4.db and logins.json from `/.mozilla/firefox/` for exfiltration.
BlackEnergy has used a plug-in to gather credentials from web browsers including FireFox, Google Chrome, and Internet Explorer.
H1N1 dumps usernames and passwords from Firefox, Internet Explorer, and Outlook.

techniques.name: Windows Credential Manager
techniques.summary: Adversaries may acquire credentials from the Windows Credential Manager.

procedures.text: OilRig has used credential dumping tool named VALUEVAULT to steal credentials from the Windows Credential Manager.
Stealth Falcon malware gathers passwords from the Windows Credential Vault.
Valak can use a .NET compiled module named exchgrabber to enumerate credentials from the Credential Manager.
Turla has gathered credentials from the Windows Credential Manager tool.

techniques.name: Password Managers
techniques.summary: Adversaries may acquire user credentials from third-party password managers. Password managers are applications designed to store user credentials, normally in an encrypted database.

procedures.text: Threat Group-3390 obtained a KeePass database from a compromised host.
Indrik Spider has accessed and exported passwords from password managers.
Fox Kitten has used scripts to access credential information from the KeePass database.
MarkiRAT can gather information from the Keepass password manager.

techniques.name: Cloud Secrets Management Stores
techniques.summary: Adversaries may acquire credentials from cloud-native secret management solutions such as AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, and Terraform Vault.

procedures.text: TeamPCP has used malware to exfiltrate cloud secrets from targeted environments including AWS, GCP, and Azure.
Mini Shai-Hulud has captured credentials stored in cloud secret stores.
Shai-Hulud has gathered secrets from AWS Secrets and GCP Secret Manager. Shai-Hulud has also gathered data from Azure Key Vault.
BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has a module that gathered Cloud Secrets Management Stores from password vaults within Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

techniques.name: Modify Authentication Process
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify authentication mechanisms and processes to access user credentials or enable otherwise unwarranted access to accounts.

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has modified the Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) configurations forcing devices to use less secure authentication methods and to send information to their infrastructure.
Ebury can intercept private keys using a trojanized ssh-add function.
SILENTTRINITY can create a backdoor in KeePass using a malicious config file and in TortoiseSVN using a registry hook.
Kessel has trojanized the ssh_login and user-auth_pubkey functions to steal plaintext credentials.

techniques.name: Domain Controller Authentication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may patch the authentication process on a domain controller to bypass the typical authentication mechanisms and enable access to accounts.

procedures.text: Chimera's malware has altered the NTLM authentication program on domain controllers to allow Chimera to login without a valid credential.

Skeleton Key is used to patch an enterprise domain controller authentication process with a backdoor password. It allows adversaries to bypass the standard authentication system to use a defined password for all accounts authenticating t...

techniques.name: Password Filter DLL
techniques.summary: Adversaries may register malicious password filter dynamic link libraries (DLLs) into the authentication process to acquire user credentials as they are validated.

procedures.text: Remsec harvests plain-text credentials as a password filter registered on domain controllers.
OilRig has registered a password filter DLL in order to drop malware.

Strider has registered its persistence module on domain controllers as a Windows LSA (Local System Authority) password filter to acquire credentials any time a domain, local user, or administrator logs in or changes a password.
MirrorFace has used a tool named MRSAStealer as a password filter to collect credentials on password changes.

techniques.name: Pluggable Authentication Modules
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify pluggable authentication modules (PAM) to access user credentials or enable otherwise unwarranted access to accounts.

procedures.text: Ebury can deactivate PAM modules to tamper with the sshd configuration.
Skidmap has the ability to replace the pam_unix.so file on an infected machine with its own malicious version that accepts a specific backdoor password for all users.

techniques.name: Network Device Authentication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use Patch System Image to hard code a password in the operating system, thus bypassing of native authentication mechanisms for local accounts on network devices.

procedures.text: SLOWPULSE can modify LDAP and two factor authentication flows by inspecting login credentials and forcing successful authentication if the provided password matches a chosen backdoor password.
SYNful Knock has the capability to add its own custom backdoor password when it modifies the operating system of the affected network device.
DRYHOOK has patched victim appliances authentication routines to capture credentials in plaintext as users log in.

techniques.name: Reversible Encryption
techniques.summary: An adversary may abuse Active Directory authentication encryption properties to gain access to credentials on Windows systems.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms to enable persistent access to compromised accounts.

procedures.text: After compromising user accounts, Scattered Spider registers their own MFA tokens.
SLOWPULSE can insert malicious logic to bypass RADIUS and ACE two factor authentication (2FA) flows if a designated attacker-supplied password is provided.
The AADInternals `Set-AADIntUserMFA` command can be used to disable MFA for a specified user.

techniques.name: Hybrid Identity

techniques.name: Network Provider DLL
techniques.summary: Adversaries may register malicious network provider dynamic link libraries (DLLs) to capture cleartext user credentials during the authentication process.

techniques.name: Conditional Access Policies
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify conditional access policies to enable persistent access to compromised accounts.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has added additional trusted locations to Azure AD conditional access policies.
Storm-0501 has registered their own MFA method, and leveraged a victim hybrid joined server to circumvent Conditional Access Policies.

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to position themselves between two or more networked devices using an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) technique to support follow-on behaviors such as Network Sniffing, Transmitted Data Manipula...
