techniques.name: DNS/Passive DNS
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search DNS data for information about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: WHOIS
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search public WHOIS data for information about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Digital Certificates
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search public digital certificate data for information about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: CDNs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search content delivery network (CDN) data about victims that can be used during targeting. CDNs allow an organization to host content from a distributed, load balanced array of servers.

techniques.name: Scan Databases
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search within public scan databases for information about victims that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: APT41 uses the Chinese website fofa.su, similar to the Shodan scanning service, for passive scanning of victims.
Volt Typhoon has used FOFA, Shodan, and Censys to search for exposed victim infrastructure.

techniques.name: Search Closed Sources
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search and gather information about victims from closed (e.g., paid, private, or otherwise not freely available) sources that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: EXOTIC LILY has searched for information on targeted individuals on business databases including RocketReach and CrunchBase.

techniques.name: Threat Intel Vendors
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search private data from threat intelligence vendors for information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Purchase Technical Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may purchase technical information about victims that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: LAPSUS$ has purchased credentials and session tokens from criminal underground forums.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send phishing messages to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: Scattered Spider has used a combination of credential phishing and social engineering to capture one-time-password (OTP) codes.
ZIRCONIUM targeted presidential campaign staffers with credential phishing e-mails.
Kimsuky has used tailored spearphishing emails to gather victim information including contat lists to identify additional targets.
APT28 has used spearphishing to compromise credentials.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages via third-party services to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: NIMBUS MANTICORE has corresponded and disseminated links to victims through social media.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages with a malicious attachment to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: Dragonfly has used spearphishing with Microsoft Office attachments to enable harvesting of user credentials.
Star Blizzard has sent emails to establish rapport with targets eventually sending messages with attachments containing links to credential-stealing sites.
Sidewinder has sent e-mails with malicious attachments that lead victims to credential harvesting websites.
SideCopy has crafted generic lures for spam campaigns to collect emails and credentials for targeting efforts.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Link
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages with a malicious link to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: Sidewinder has sent e-mails with malicious links to credential harvesting websites.
Scattered Spider has used domains mirroring corporate login portals to socially engineer victims into providing credentials.
Mustang Panda has delivered web bugs to profile their intended targets.
Sandworm Team has crafted spearphishing emails with hyperlinks designed to trick unwitting recipients into revealing their account credentials.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Voice
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use voice communications to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: LAPSUS$ has called victims' help desk to convince the support personnel to reset a privileged account’s credentials.
Scattered Spider has used help desk voice-based phishing and also called employees at target organizations and compelled them to navigate to fake login portals using adversary-in-the-middle toolkits.

techniques.name: Network Boundary Bridging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bridge network boundaries by compromising perimeter network devices or internal devices responsible for network segmentation.

procedures.text: APT41 used `NATBypass` to bypass firewall restrictions and to access compromised systems via RDP.
Salt Typhoon has abused peer connections to exfiltrate data.

techniques.name: Network Address Translation Traversal
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bridge network boundaries by modifying a network device’s Network Address Translation (NAT) configuration.

techniques.name: Weaken Encryption
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise a network device’s encryption capability in order to bypass encryption that would otherwise protect data communications.

techniques.name: Reduce Key Space
techniques.summary: Adversaries may reduce the level of effort required to decrypt data transmitted over the network by reducing the cipher strength of encrypted communications.

techniques.name: Disable Crypto Hardware
techniques.summary: Adversaries disable a network device’s dedicated hardware encryption, which may enable them to leverage weaknesses in software encryption in order to reduce the effort involved in collecting, manipulating, and exfiltr...

techniques.name: Modify System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may make changes to the operating system of embedded network devices to weaken defenses and provide new capabilities for themselves.

procedures.text: DRYHOOK has modified the Ivanti Connect Secure VPN authentication Perl module `DSAuth.pm` by reading its contents in the buffer, then finding and replacing select lines of code.

techniques.name: Patch System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the operating system of a network device to introduce new capabilities or weaken existing defenses.

procedures.text: SYNful Knock is malware that is inserted into a network device by patching the operating system image.

techniques.name: Downgrade System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install an older version of the operating system of a network device to weaken security.

techniques.name: Data from Configuration Repository
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect data related to managed devices from configuration repositories. Configuration repositories are used by management systems in order to configure, manage, and control data on remote systems.

techniques.name: SNMP (MIB Dump)
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target the Management Information Base (MIB) to collect and/or mine valuable information in a network managed using Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP).

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has enumerated device configuration using SNMP and gathered data stored in the Managed Information Base on target devices.

techniques.name: Network Device Configuration Dump
techniques.summary: Adversaries may access network configuration files to collect sensitive data about the device and the network. The network configuration is a file containing parameters that determine the operation of the device.

procedures.text: GlassWorm has gathered data pertaining to VPN configurations. GlassWorm has also targeted locally stored data on macOS located in `/Library/Application Support/Fortinet/FortiClient/conf/vpn.plist`.
Salt Typhoon has attempted to acquire credentials by dumping network device configurations. Salt Typhoon has also obtained data using RANCID.

techniques.name: Forge Web Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forge credential materials that can be used to gain access to web applications or Internet services.

techniques.name: Web Cookies
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forge web cookies that can be used to gain access to web applications or Internet services.

techniques.name: SAML Tokens
techniques.summary: An adversary may forge SAML tokens with any permissions claims and lifetimes if they possess a valid SAML token-signing certificate.

procedures.text: AADInternals can be used to create SAML tokens using the AD Federated Services token signing certificate.

techniques.name: Stage Capabilities
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload, install, or otherwise set up capabilities that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: Mustang Panda has used servers under their control to validate tracking pixels sent to phishing victims.

techniques.name: Upload Malware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload malware to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting.

procedures.text: Sandworm Team staged compromised versions of legitimate software installers in forums to enable initial access to executing user.
TA2541 has uploaded malware to various platforms including Google Drive, Pastetext, Sharetext, and GitHub.
Earth Lusca has staged malware and malicious files on compromised web servers, GitHub, and Google Drive.
Mustang Panda has hosted malicious payloads on DropBox including PlugX.

techniques.name: Upload Tool
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload tools to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting.

procedures.text: Medusa Group has utilized a file hosting service called filemail[.]com to host a zip file that contained a RMM service such as ConnectWise.
Threat Group-3390 has staged tools, including gsecdump and WCE, on previously compromised websites.

techniques.name: Install Digital Certificate
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install SSL/TLS certificates that can be used during targeting. SSL/TLS certificates are files that can be installed on servers to enable secure communications between systems.

procedures.text: Sea Turtle captured legitimate SSL certificates from victim organizations and installed these on Sea Turtle-controlled infrastructure to enable subsequent adversary-in-the-middle operations.

techniques.name: Drive-by Target
techniques.summary: Adversaries may prepare an operational environment to infect systems that visit a website over the normal course of browsing.

procedures.text: Transparent Tribe has set up websites with malicious hyperlinks and iframes to infect targeted victims with Crimson, njRAT, and other malicious tools.
LuminousMoth has redirected compromised machines to an actor-controlled webpage through HTML injection.
Dragonfly has compromised websites to redirect traffic and to host exploit kits.
CURIUM used strategic website compromise to fingerprint then target victims.

techniques.name: Link Target
techniques.summary: Adversaries may put in place resources that are referenced by a link that can be used during targeting.

procedures.text: FIN7 has created a fake link that redirected to an adversary-controlled Dropbox that downloaded the malicious executable.
LuminousMoth has created a link to a Dropbox file that has been used in their spear-phishing operations.

NIMBUS MANTICORE had registered domains that would point to a typo-squatted domain used to deliver malicious payloads. NIMBUS MANTICORE has also pre-shared credentials with a link to spoofed phishing login pages that enable the download...

Silent Librarian has cloned victim organization login pages and staged them for later use in credential harvesting campaigns. Silent Librarian has also made use of a variety of URL shorteners for these staged websites.

techniques.name: SEO Poisoning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison mechanisms that influence search engine optimization (SEO) to further lure staged capabilities towards potential victims.

procedures.text: NIMBUS MANTICORE has utilized Search Engine Optimization (SEO) poisoning to deliver malware to unsuspecting victims. NIMBUS MANTICORE has also registered dozens of domains that link to a typosquatted domain to generate link-based reputat...
Mustard Tempest has poisoned search engine results to return fake software updates in order to distribute malware.

techniques.name: AI Result Poisoning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate publicly accessible web content to influence generative AI systems or AI-powered search engines into retrieving, citing, or recommending attacker-controlled information.

techniques.name: Container Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse a container administration service to execute commands within a container.

procedures.text: TeamTNT executed Hildegard through the kubelet API run command and by executing commands on running containers.
Peirates can use `kubectl` or the Kubernetes API to run commands.
Hildegard was executed through the kubelet API run command and by executing commands on running containers.
CanisterWorm can deploy privileged DaemonSets in Kubernetes clusters for data wiping using kubectl.

techniques.name: Deploy Container
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deploy a container into an environment to facilitate execution or evade defenses.

procedures.text: Kinsing was run through a deployed Ubuntu container.
Salt Typhoon has enabled Linux containers in victim network device environments using `guestshell enable`.
TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can deploy a pod in Kubernetes containers to run a script to establish persistence.

TeamTNT has deployed different types of containers into victim environments to facilitate execution. TeamTNT has also transferred cryptocurrency mining software to Kubernetes clusters discovered within local IP address ranges.

techniques.name: Escape to Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may break out of a container or virtualized environment to gain access to the underlying host.

procedures.text: Peirates can gain a reverse shell on a host node by mounting the Kubernetes hostPath.
Doki’s container was configured to bind the host root directory.
Siloscape maps the host’s C drive to the container by creating a global symbolic link to the host through the calling of NtSetInformationSymbolicLink .
TeamTNT has deployed privileged containers that mount the filesystem of victim machine.

techniques.name: Build Image on Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may build a container image directly on a host to bypass defenses that monitor for the retrieval of malicious images from a public registry.

techniques.name: Container and Resource Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to discover containers and other resources that are available within a containers environment.

procedures.text: Peirates can enumerate Kubernetes pods in a given namespace.

CanisterWorm has performed environment fingerprinting to identify Kubernetes clusters. CanisterWorm has also searched for Kubernetes pods using the command ` os.path.exists("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount") or "KUBERNETES_...
TeamTNT has checked for running containers with docker ps and for specific container names with docker inspect . TeamTNT has also searched for Kubernetes pods running in a local network.
Hildegard has used masscan to search for kubelets and the kubelet API for additional running containers.

techniques.name: System Location Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information in an attempt to calculate the geographical location of a victim host.

procedures.text: DarkWatchman can identity the OS locale of a compromised host.
Gootloader can use IP geolocation to determine if the person browsing to a compromised site is within a targeted territory such as the US, Canada, Germany, and South Korea.
PlugX has obtained the location of the victim device by leveraging `GetSystemDefaultLCID`.
SideCopy has identified the country location of a compromised host.

techniques.name: System Language Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about the system language of a victim in order to infer the geographical location of that host.

procedures.text: Cuckoo Stealer can check the systems `LANG` environmental variable to prevent infecting devices from Armenia (`hy_AM`), Belarus (`be_BY`), Kazakhstan (`kk_KZ`), Russia (`ru_RU`), and Ukraine (`uk_UA`).
MarkiRAT can use the GetKeyboardLayout API to check if a compromised host's keyboard is set to Persian.
XCSSET uses AppleScript to check the host's language and location with the command user locale of (get system info) .
Cuba can check if Russian language is installed on the infected machine by using the function GetKeyboardLayoutList .

techniques.name: Group Policy Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information on Group Policy settings to identify paths for privilege escalation, security measures applied within a domain, and to discover patterns in domain objects that can be manipulated or...

procedures.text: LunarWeb can capture information on group policy settings
DUSTTRAP can identify victim environment Group Policy information.
BloodHound has the ability to collect local admin information via GPO.
Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover Group Policy details using the gpresult command.

techniques.name: Cloud Storage Object Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate objects in cloud storage infrastructure.

procedures.text: TruffleHog can enumerate cloud storage environments including Amazon Web Service (AWS) S3 buckets and Google Cloud Storage buckets.
Pacu can enumerate AWS storage services, such as S3 buckets and Elastic Block Store volumes.
Peirates can list AWS S3 buckets.
ShinyHunters has used Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) Browser and WinSCP to access S3 objects.

techniques.name: Reflective Code Loading
techniques.summary: Adversaries may reflectively load code into a process in order to conceal the execution of malicious payloads.

procedures.text: BADHATCH can copy a large byte array of 64-bit shellcode into process memory and execute it with a call to `CreateThread`.
WhisperGate's downloader can reverse its third stage file bytes and reflectively load the file as a .NET assembly.
Uroburos has the ability to load new modules directly into memory using its `Load Modules Mem` command.
SILENTTRINITY can run a .NET executable within the memory of a sacrificial process by loading the CLR.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms and gain access to accounts by generating MFA requests sent to users.

procedures.text: APT29 has used repeated MFA requests to gain access to victim accounts.
Scattered Spider has used multifactor authentication (MFA) fatigue by sending repeated MFA authentication requests to targets.
LAPSUS$ has spammed target users with MFA prompts in the hope that the legitimate user will grant necessary approval.

techniques.name: Debugger Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid debuggers. Debuggers are typically used by defenders to trace and/or analyze the execution of potential malware payloads.

procedures.text: Lumma Stealer has checked for debugger strings by invoking `GetForegroundWindow` and looks for strings containing “x32dbg”, “x64dbg”, “windbg”, “ollydbg”, “dnspy”, “immunity debugger”, “hyperdbg”, “debug”, “debugger”, “cheat engine”, “ch...
AsyncRAT can use the `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent` function to detect the presence of a debugger.
PlugX has made calls to Windows API `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent` and exits if it detects a debugger.
StealBit can detect it is being run in the context of a debugger.

techniques.name: Plist File Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify property list files (plist files) to enable other malicious activity, while also potentially evading and bypassing system defenses.

procedures.text: Cuckoo Stealer can create and populate property list (plist) files to enable execution.

In older versions, XCSSET uses the plutil command to modify the LSUIElement , DFBundleDisplayName , and CFBundleIdentifier keys in the /Contents/Info.plist file to change how XCSSET is visible on the system. In later versions, XCSSET lev...

techniques.name: Serverless Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse serverless computing, integration, and automation services to execute arbitrary code in cloud environments.

procedures.text: Pacu can create malicious Lambda functions.

techniques.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal or forge certificates used for authentication to access remote systems or resources. Digital certificates are often used to sign and encrypt messages and/or files.

procedures.text: AADInternals can create and export various authentication certificates, including those associated with Azure AD joined/registered devices.
NIMBUS MANTICORE has stolen and leveraged vulnerable Active Directory Certificate Services templates to impersonate higher-privileged user accounts.
Mini Shai-Hulud has collected victim client certificates to assist in signed authentication assertion with Azure environments.
APT29 has abused misconfigured AD CS certificate templates to impersonate admin users and create additional authentication certificates.

techniques.name: Acquire Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may purchase or otherwise acquire an existing access to a target system or network.

procedures.text: Medusa Group has purchased user credentials and other sensitive data from Initial Access Brokers (IABs).

techniques.name: Cloud Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse cloud management services to execute commands within virtual machines.

procedures.text: APT29 has used Azure Run Command and Azure Admin-on-Behalf-of (AOBO) to execute code on virtual machines.
VOID MANTICORE has abused built-in remote wipe or factory reset commands to wipe devices managed within an organization’s Cloud management solution impacting laptops, servers, and mobile devices.
AADInternals can execute commands on Azure virtual machines using the VM agent.
Pacu can run commands on EC2 instances using AWS Systems Manager Run Command.

techniques.name: Device Driver Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate local device drivers on a victim host.

procedures.text: HOPLIGHT can enumerate device drivers located in the registry at `HKLM\Software\WBEM\WDM`.
INC Ransomware can verify the presence of specific drivers on compromised hosts including Microsoft Print to PDF and Microsoft XPS Document Writer.
Medusa Group has queried drivers on the victim device through the command `driverquery`.
Remsec has a plugin to detect active drivers of some security products.

techniques.name: Power Settings
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impair a system's ability to hibernate, reboot, or shut down in order to extend access to infected machines.

procedures.text: Line Runner used CVE-2024-20353 to trigger victim devices to reboot, in the process unzipping and installing the Line Dancer payload.
Line Dancer can modify the crash dump process on infected machines to skip crash dump generation and proceed directly to device reboot for both persistence and forensic evasion purposes.

techniques.name: Log Enumeration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate system and service logs to find useful data.

procedures.text: BeaverTail has identified .ldb and .log files stored in browser extension directories for collection and exfiltration.
APT5 has used the BLOODMINE utility to parse and extract information from Pulse Secure Connect logs.
Ember Bear has enumerated SECURITY and SYSTEM log files during intrusions.
Volt Typhoon has used `wevtutil.exe` and the PowerShell command `Get-EventLog security` to enumerate Windows logs to search for successful logons.

techniques.name: Financial Theft
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal monetary resources from targets through extortion, social engineering, technical theft, or other methods aimed at their own financial gain at the expense of the availability of these resources fo...

procedures.text: APT38 has conducted cryptocurrency theft.
INC Ransom has stolen and encrypted victim's data in order to extort payment for keeping it private or decrypting it.
Embargo has been leveraged in double-extortion ransomware, exfiltrating files then encrypting them, to prompt victims to pay a ransom.
InvisibleFerret has searched the victim device credentials and files commonly associated with cryptocurrency wallets.

techniques.name: Content Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access and continuously communicate with victims by injecting malicious content into systems through online network traffic.

procedures.text: Disco has achieved initial access and execution through content injection into DNS, HTTP, and SMB replies to targeted hosts that redirect them to download malicious files.
MoustachedBouncer has injected content into DNS, HTTP, and SMB replies to redirect specifically-targeted victims to a fake Windows Update page to download malware.

techniques.name: Hide Infrastructure
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate network traffic in order to hide and evade detection of their C2 infrastructure.

procedures.text: ZIRCONIUM has utilized an ORB (operational relay box) network – consisting compromised devices such as small office and home office (SOHO) routers, IoT devices, and leased virtual private servers (VPS) – to obfuscate the origin of C2 tra...
JumbledPath can use a chain of jump hosts to communicate with compromised devices to obscure actor infrastructure.
DarkGate command and control includes hard-coded domains in the malware masquerading as legitimate services such as Akamai CDN or Amazon Web Services.
APT29 uses compromised residential endpoints, typically within the same ISP IP address range, as proxies to hide the true source of C2 traffic.

techniques.name: Modify Cloud Resource Hierarchy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to modify hierarchical structures in infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environments in order to evade defenses.

techniques.name: Email Bombing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may flood targeted email addresses with an overwhelming volume of messages. This may bury legitimate emails in a flood of spam and disrupt business operations.

procedures.text: Storm-1811 has deployed large volumes of non-malicious email spam to victims in order to prompt follow-on interactions with the threat actor posing as IT support or helpdesk to resolve the problem.

techniques.name: Exclusive Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries who successfully compromise a system may attempt to maintain persistence by “closing the door” behind them – in other words, by preventing other threat actors from initially accessing or maintaining a foot...

techniques.name: Wi-Fi Networks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain initial access to target systems by connecting to wireless networks.

procedures.text: APT28 has exploited open Wi-Fi access points for initial access to target devices using the network.

techniques.name: Cloud Application Integration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by leveraging OAuth application integrations in a software-as-a-service environment.

techniques.name: Virtual Machine Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to enumerate running virtual machines (VMs) after gaining access to a host or hypervisor.

procedures.text: PureCrypter can identify virtual machines by querying the WMI object Win32_ComputerSystem for manufacturer and model and check it against the regular expression Microsoft|VMWare|Virtual.
UNC3886 has used scripts to enumerate ESXi hypervisors and their guest VMs.
Qilin can detect virtual machine environments including ESXi hosts, datacenters, and clusters within vCenter environments.
VIRTUALPITA can target specific guest virtual machines for script execution.

techniques.name: Input Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may simulate keystrokes on a victim’s computer by various means to perform any type of action on behalf of the user, such as launching the command interpreter using keyboard shortcuts, typing an inline scr...

procedures.text: FIN7 has used malicious USBs to emulate keystrokes to launch PowerShell to download and execute malware from the adversary's server.

techniques.name: ESXi Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse ESXi administration services to execute commands on guest machines hosted within an ESXi virtual environment.

procedures.text: VIRTUALPITA can execute commands on guest virtual machines from compromised ESXi hypervisors.
UNC3886 used `vmtoolsd.exe` to run commands on guest virtual machines from a compromised ESXi host.
The Gentlemen Ransomware has utilized ESXi administration commands to include `vmkfstools` to modify the compromised system.

techniques.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate continuous integration / continuous development (CI/CD) processes by injecting malicious code into the build process.

procedures.text: APT38 has poisoned npm packages with fake runtime dependencies to trigger execution of malicious payloads on developer endpoints or continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) systems during npm installation or update.
Shai-Hulud has also leveraged GitHub actions from stolen accounts in order to create a malicious Github workflow within `.github/workflows/discussion.yaml`.
Mini Shai-Hulud has utilized Github Actions to propagate through the use of triggered workflows.
CanisterWorm has leveraged stolen tokens from Trivy users to publish itself across over 46 npm packages.

techniques.name: Delay Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various time-based methods to evade detection and analysis.

procedures.text: TeamPCP Cloud Stealer has leveraged a persistence script that will sleep for five minutes before additional execution.
Kimsuky has utilized the Sleep function to ensure execution of scripts.
MuddyViper has the ability to sleep for a certain amount of time, with the default being one minute.
TONESHELL has the ability to pause operations for a specified duration prior to follow-on execution of activities.

techniques.name: Selective Exclusion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may intentionally exclude certain files, folders, directories, file types, or system components from encryption or tampering during a ransomware or malicious payload execution.

procedures.text: LazyWiper can enumerate the hostname of the system to determine if it is a domain controller and exclude it from being wiped if so.
Medusa Ransomware has avoided specified files, file extensions and folders to ensure successful execution of the payload and continued operations of the impacted device.

DynoWiper has recursively enumerated directories with the exception of the following: System32, Windows, Program Files, Program Files(x86), Temp, Recycle.Bin, $Recycle.Bin, Boot, PerfLogs, AppData, Documents and Settings.
InvisibleFerret has the capability to scan for file names, file extensions, and avoids pre-designated path names and file types.

techniques.name: Local Storage Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate local drives, disks, and/or volumes and their attributes like total or free space and volume serial number.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has searched for disk partition and logical volume information.
SLOTHFULMEDIA has collected disk information from a victim machine.
ZeroCleare can use the `IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY_EX`, `IOCTL_DISK_GET_DRIVE_GEOMETRY`, and `IOCTL_DISK_GET_LENGTH_INFO` system calls to compute disk size.
MoonWind can obtain the number of drives on the victim machine.

techniques.name: Search Threat Vendor Data
techniques.summary: Threat actors may seek information/indicators from closed or open threat intelligence sources gathered about their own campaigns, as well as those conducted by other adversaries that may align with their target indust...

procedures.text: UNC3886 has replaced indicators mentioned in open-source threat intelligence publications at times under a week after their release.
Contagious Interview has registered accounts with Threat Intelligence vendor services to check for reporting associated with their infrastructure and to evaluate new potential infrastructure.

techniques.name: Query Public AI Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may query publicly accessible artificial intelligence (AI) services, such as large language models (LLMs), to support targeting and operations.

procedures.text: APT42 has leveraged LLMs to search for official emails to build target lists, and conduct reconnaissance on potential business partners.
Kimsuky has used LLMs to identify think tanks, government organizations, and experts to inform targeting for spearphishing campaigns.

techniques.name: Generate Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or generate content to support targeting and operations.

procedures.text: BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR has created a skills file titled `AI LATERAL_SUGGESTIONS.md` that included tables mapped with harvested credentials with potential victim internal servers.

techniques.name: Written Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or tailor written materials to support targeting and malicious operations.

procedures.text: APT-C-36 has generated email content impersonating official notifications and documents that direct victims to execute malicious payloads.

Kali365 has generated tailored branded phishing lures to target victims utilizing a myriad of reputable services and brands that entice users to interact with the content. Kali365 has also been enabled with AI such as Claude Sonnet that...
Contagious Interview has created fake social media accounts such as LinkedIn and Telegram accounts for their targeting efforts.
The Gentlemen has utilized branded code and ransom notes.

techniques.name: Audio-Visual Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or manipulate audio, image, and video content to support targeting and malicious operations.

procedures.text: APT38 has created fictitious profiles on social media utilizing fake photos and personas to entice users to engage in the schemes.

NIMBUS MANTICORE has generated fictitious job-related themed websites that entice users to interact and launch malicious actions. NIMBUS MANTICORE has also utilized decoy documents and files to provide a sense of legitimacy to the user....
The Gentlemen has leveraged a branded graphic that is placed on the systems desktop wallpaper that symbolizes the association of malicious activity to the group.
APT-C-36 has used phishing pages appearing like legitimate banking login portals to compromise credentials.

techniques.name: Social Engineering
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use social engineering techniques to influence users to take actions that result in unauthorized access, approval of changes, disclosure of sensitive information, or execution of adversary-supplied ins...

procedures.text: ShinyHunters has used social engineering to demand payment from victims.

techniques.name: Impersonation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impersonate a trusted person or organization in order to persuade and trick a target into performing some action on their behalf.

procedures.text: Star Blizzard has registered impersonation email accounts to spoof experts in a particular field or individuals and organizations affiliated with the intended target.
RustyWater has impersonated TMCell (Altyn Asyr CJSC), the primary mobile operator in Turkmenistan, sending phishing emails with the email domain `info@tmcell`.

Kimsuky has also impersonated legitimate people, such as a foreign advisor, an embassy employee, and a think tank employee. Kimsuky has also purported to be a Japanese diplomat to communicate with the victims.
NPPSPY creates a network listener using the misspelled label logincontroll recorded to the Registry key HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\NetworkProvider\\Order .

techniques.name: Email Spoofing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may fake, or spoof, a sender’s identity by modifying the value of relevant email headers in order to establish contact with victims under false pretenses.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable, degrade, or tamper with security tools or applications (e.g., endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools, intrusion detection systems (IDS), antivirus, logging agents, sensors, etc.) to impai...

procedures.text: KOCTOPUS will attempt to delete or disable all Registry keys and scheduled tasks related to Microsoft Security Defender and Security Essentials.
SplatCloak has identified and disabled API callback features of Windows Defender and Kaspersky.

macOS.OSAMiner has searched for the Activity Monitor process in the System Events process list and kills the process if running. macOS.OSAMiner also searches the operating system's `install.log` for apps matching its hardcoded list, kill...
MegaCortex was used to kill endpoint security processes.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Windows Event Log to limit data that can be leveraged for detections and audits. Windows Event Log records user and system activity such as login attempts and process creation.

procedures.text: Wevtutil can be used to disable specific event logs on the system.
Magic Hound has executed scripts to disable the event log service.
Threat Group-3390 has used appcmd.exe to disable logging on a victim server.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
techniques.summary: An adversary may disable or modify cloud logging capabilities and integrations to limit what data is collected on their activities and avoid detection.

procedures.text: Pacu can disable or otherwise restrict various AWS logging services, such as AWS CloudTrail and VPC flow logs.
APT29 has disabled Purview Audit on targeted accounts prior to stealing emails from Microsoft 365 tenants.

techniques.name: Modify or Spoof Tool UI
techniques.summary: Adversaries may spoof or manipulate security tool user interfaces (UIs) to falsely indicate tools are functioning normally and delay detection and response.

procedures.text: NIMBUS MANTICORE has prompted victims with fake warnings and error messages to appear as legitimate failures to reduce user suspicion.
APT38 has displayed a fake “system update complete” dialog to the user following successful deployment of malicious payloads.

PHASEJAM has prevented legitimate Ivanti Connect Secure system upgrades by intercepting the upgrade command and rendering fake HTML upgrade progress bar through a function called `processUpgradeDisplay()` which allowed the compromised de...

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Linux Audit system to hide malicious activity and avoid detection. Linux admins use the Linux Audit system to track security-relevant information on a system.

procedures.text: Ebury disables OpenSSH, system (`systemd`), and audit logs (`/sbin/auditd`) when the backdoor is active.

techniques.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may clear Windows Event Logs to hide the activity of an intrusion. Windows Event Logs are a record of a computer's alerts and notifications.

procedures.text: Apostle will attempt to delete all event logs on a victim machine following file wipe activity.
BlackCat can clear Windows event logs using `wevtutil.exe`.
FinFisher clears the system event logs using OpenEventLog/ClearEventLog APIs .
The BlackEnergy component KillDisk is capable of deleting Windows Event Logs.

techniques.name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may clear system logs to hide evidence of an intrusion. macOS and Linux both keep track of system or user-initiated actions via system logs.

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has cleared logs including .bash_history, auth.log, lastlog, wtmp, and btmp.
UPSTYLE clears error logs after reading embedded commands for execution.
Proton removes logs from /var/logs and /Library/logs .
MacMa can clear possible malware traces such as application logs.

techniques.name: Impair Autonomous Defenses
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use methods like Indirect Prompt Injection to disrupt, disable, or otherwise impair autonomous defensive capabilities such as LLM-assisted processing of malware, artifacts, or activity.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify host-based or network firewalls to impair defensive mechanisms and enable further action.

procedures.text: TeamTNT has disabled iptables .
InvisiMole has a command to disable routing and the Firewall on the victim’s machine.

Prior to executing a backdoor ToddyCat has run `cmd /c start /b netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="SGAccessInboundRule" dir=in protocol=udp action=allow localport=49683` to allow the targeted system to receive UDP packets on port...
THINCRUST can use the Django python module "django.views.decorators.csrf” along with the decorator “csrf_exempt” within victim firewalls to disable cross-site request forgery protections.

techniques.name: Cloud Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify a firewall within a cloud environment to bypass controls that limit access to cloud resources.

procedures.text: Pacu can allowlist IP addresses in AWS GuardDuty.

techniques.name: Network Device Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable network device-based firewall mechanisms entirely or add, delete, or modify particular rules in order to bypass controls limiting network usage.

procedures.text: Salt Typhoon has modified the network firewalls access control lists to add IP addresses to bypass security policies and maintain access.
APT38 have created firewall exemptions on specific ports, including ports 443, 6443, 8443, and 9443.
Grandoreiro can block the Deibold Warsaw GAS Tecnologia security tool at the firewall level.
Cyclops Blink can modify the Linux iptables firewall to enable C2 communication on network devices via a stored list of port numbers.

techniques.name: Windows Host Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Windows host firewall to bypass controls limiting network usage.

procedures.text: BADCALL disables the Windows firewall before binding to a port.
DarkComet can disable Security Center functions like the Windows Firewall.
MirrorFace can modify the system firewall to allow communication to certain ports.
Remsec can add or remove applications or ports on the Windows firewall or disable it entirely.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Defense Impairment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in security software, infrastructure, or defensive components to degrade, disable, or otherwise continue to impair their ability to prevent, detect, or respond to malicious acti...

techniques.name: Safe Mode Boot
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Windows safe mode to disable endpoint defenses. Safe mode starts up the Windows operating system with a limited set of drivers and services.

procedures.text: Embargo has used a DLL variant of MDeployer to disable security solutions through Safe Mode.
AvosLocker can restart a compromised machine in safe mode.
REvil can force a reboot in safe mode with networking.
Black Basta can reboot victim machines in safe mode with networking via `bcdedit /set safeboot network`.

techniques.name: Downgrade Attack
techniques.summary: Adversaries may downgrade or use a version of system features that may be outdated, vulnerable, and/or does not support updated security controls.

procedures.text: The Gentlemen Ransomware has used the following command to re-enable SMB1: `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol -NoRestart`.
SILENTTRINITY can downgrade NTLM to capture NTLM hashes.
BlackByte Ransomware enables SMBv1 during execution.

techniques.name: Prevent Command History Logging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impair command history logging to hide commands they run on a compromised system.

procedures.text: Line Dancer can disable syslog on compromised devices.
Sea Turtle unset the Bash and MySQL history files on victim systems.
BRICKSTORM has impaired command logging through the use of `dev/null` which prevents generating output from the command and does not wait for input.
UNC3886 has tampered with and disabled logging services on targeted systems.

techniques.name: Anti-Automation Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to evade or complete automation checks. Automation checks distinguish human users from bot traffic and prevent bots from reaching the web pages protected by automation checks.

techniques.name: Automate CAPTCHA Completion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to use bots to successfully solve CAPTCHA challenges. CAPTCHA challenges are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages.

techniques.name: Avoid CAPTCHA
techniques.summary: Adversaries may avoid CAPTCHA challenges by mimicking human behavior. Automation tests, such as CAPTCHA, are typically used by defenders to detect and prevent bot and spam traffic from accessing protected webpages.

techniques.name: Steal Application Specific Passwords
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal Application Specific Passwords (ASPs) to gain access to Valid Accounts, bypassing multifactor authentication (MFA) methods.

procedures.text: APT42 has stolen application specific passwords in order to bypass MFA requirements to include victim environments who leverage the Microsoft App Password feature.

techniques.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deliver malicious prompts to an LLM indirectly by embedding the prompts in content that the adversary expects may be processed by an LLM.

techniques.name: Direct Prompt Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may input malicious prompts directly into an LLM’s user interface.

techniques.name: AI-Enabled Exfiltration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize Direct Prompt Injection, Indirect Prompt Injection or other methods to instruct enterprise AI agents to exfiltrate data.
